## D357 — A rescan re-runs the matcher on everything a person did not set: per item, per library, and for all of them

**Decided** (2026-10-27), by the project owner, after the matcher's fix for a film named exactly as
the file and another with an article ("Crowd", 2022, matched to "The Crowd" of the same
year, the owner's staging) reached only titles matched after it: "we're likely to encounter other
unhandled cases that misidentify things during beta and even after release, requiring us to ship
fixes." A fix to the matcher reaches the library only when it re-runs; this is how it re-runs.

1. **Three buttons, for an admin.** "Rescan everything" on the Libraries page, over every library
   whose kind is films or series (not mixed or other); "Rescan" on each such library; and "Rescan
   this" on a film's or a series' page. A series is rescanned as the one thing identified, its
   episodes following it (D209).
2. **A rescan is a scan, then a re-match.** The scope's files are scanned as a manual scan scans them
   (new, changed and gone files found; a file unchanged on disk is not probed again), and then the
   matcher runs again on every film and series in the scope, as it would on one never matched: the
   name and year read from the files and their NFOs, the provider searched again (a clear match
   keeps no candidates, D301), the matcher as it now is settling it.
3. **What a person set through the app is left alone:** a match a person chose (D172, D301 §2),
   every field a person edited (D305's overrides), and anything else set in the app. A match the
   matcher guessed and no one confirmed is re-matched like any other.
4. **A different answer replaces the old one, without review** (the owner: "Just change it. If it's
   wrong, they already have the means to manually fix it"): the new match is kept as the matcher's
   own would be, a guess marked as one where it is a guess (D301), and corrected from the title's
   page as any match is. What a person watched stays theirs across the change; the build says where
   each such record is kept and shows it survives.
5. **It runs in the background**, as jobs (D231), the Libraries page showing its progress; a second
   press while one runs over the same scope adds nothing. It costs one provider search per film or
   series, and a fetch for each whose match changed, within the provider's limits.
6. **Each change is logged:** the item, its old match and its new one, and what settled it (which of
   the matcher's tiers, or a guess), and each run's totals (items re-matched, changed, left alone,
   unsettled), so a report of a wrong match after a rescan is explained from the log alone.

**Verification owed:** staging's "Crowd" (2022), matched to "The Crowd" before the fix
, is left as it is, so that this decision's first build is checked on it: after "Rescan
this" it is the film named "Crowd".

**Proven by:**
- 1: TestRescan_EveryLibraryOfFilmsOrSeriesAndNoOther, TestRescan_OneItemRescansItsFilesAndRematchesIt, TestRescan_IsForAnAdminOnly, TestRescan_ASeriesIsMatchedAgainAndItsEpisodesFollow, web/apps/web/src/libraries.test.tsx and web/apps/web/src/rescan.test.tsx (the buttons)
- 2: TestRescan_ScansThenRematchesFromTheFilesNameAndYear, TestRescan_AFileUnchangedOnDiskIsNotProbedAgain, TestRescan_AFilmItsSearchNoLongerSettlesIsNamedFromItsFileAgain
- 3: TestRescan_LeavesAPersonsChoiceAndEditedFieldsAlone, TestRescan_RematchesAnUnconfirmedGuess
- 4: TestRescan_ADifferentMatchReplacesTheOld, TestRescan_ASeriesIsMatchedAgainAndItsEpisodesFollow, TestRescan_WhatAPersonWatchedSurvivesAChangedMatch
- 5: TestRescan_ASecondPressWhileOneRunsAddsNothing, TestRescan_IsForAnAdminOnly (the Libraries page's progress)
- 6: TestRescan_LogsEachChangedMatchAndTheRunsTotals

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-27.

**Build note** (2026-10-27, staging's check owed, above): the rescans
(`internal/core/identify/rescan.go`), each item's match again (`rematch.go`) from what its files say,
read by the pass with its match set aside (`files_say.go`: the stored name after a match is the
provider's, so the file's name and year are read again from the paths and NFOs); the scan of a
library, or of the folders holding one item's files (`internal/core/library/rescan_scans.go`); the
endpoints `POST /libraries/rescan`, `POST /libraries/{id}/rescan`, `POST /items/{id}/rescan` and each
library's `rescan` progress on `GET /libraries` (`internal/core/api/rescans.go`); the buttons
(`libraries.tsx`, `match-correction.tsx`). What a person watched is kept by file (`play_position`,
`play_span`, `play_event`; `progress_hide` by item), and a rescan keeps the item's title and its
files, so it stays. Decided in the build, for the owner's review: a rescan is kept in cache.db
(`rescan`, `rematch`), as a scan is, not in persistent.db, so a cache.db lost mid-rescan loses the
admin's request as it loses a scan's and the admin presses again (the alternative, a persistent
request as a refresh's, needs a migration and its golden); "Rescan everything" starts one rescan a
library; a library's matches queue in the background and one item's at a person's priority; "Rescan
this" on a film in a library being rescanned, or a second press, adds nothing.

## D358 — A cast asks the receiving device first: "‹Device› wants to play ‹Film› here", whose Play is the press that starts it with sound and full screen

**Decided** (2026-10-27), by the project owner, after casting from Firefox on a Mac to Chrome on
Linux, and to a Fire TV's Silk, played the film with no sound and out of full screen, with no
apparent way to turn the sound on (staging's log, 06:54:59 and 07:02:50 UTC: `logEvent=playedMuted`
on each receiver). A cast starts its film from a message, not a press on the receiving tab: a
browser plays sound only on a page that has been pressed (sticky activation), and puts a page full
screen only within moments of a press (transient activation)
([idiosyncrasies](../idiosyncrasies.md#a-cast-receiver-is-started-by-a-message-so-the-browser-gives-it-neither-sound-nor-full-screen)).
A press at the moment the cast arrives is the only reliable way to have both. **Amends**
[D337](#d337--casting-starts-with-a-persons-own-signed-in-devices-one-chosen-from-those-connected-now-plays-the-film-the-one-that-cast-becomes-its-remote-and-either-may-take-control-back),
whose casts started with no confirmation and whose §9 answers held the fading "Controlled from" line
enough, and the sender's hand-off at the moment it casts (D337's §9 answers: "the sender leaves its
playback at the hand-off"); keeps
[D338](#d338--a-cast-goes-to-the-devices-tab-in-front-its-receiver-keeps-a-televisions-controls-and-leaves-by-back-or-a-double-ok-and-stop-casting-returns-it-to-the-page-it-was-on).

1. **The receiver asks.** When a cast arrives, the receiving tab shows, over whatever page it is on,
   "‹Device› wants to play ‹Film› here", with **Play**, focused so a remote's OK answers it, and
   **Not now**. A click or a tap on either answers it too.
2. **Play is the press.** In Play's own handler the receiver asks for full screen and opens the
   film, which plays with sound by the activation the press gave the page. What each did is logged
   on the server: the sound allowed or refused, full screen entered or refused, and by what press.
   A desktop browser goes full screen too (the owner, 2026-10-27: "if we now have the confirmation
   prompt, making even a desktop browser go fullscreen seems fine since it's a deliberate user action
   to accept the cast"); no decision before held a desktop receiver out of full screen.
3. **Not now declines.** The sender is told the cast was declined, shows "‹Device› declined", and
   keeps playing: it hands its playback off only once the receiver has pressed Play, never as it
   casts.
4. **No answer in a minute is no.** After one minute (a justified constant) the prompt closes and
   the sender is told no one answered, and keeps playing.
5. **A refused sound can still be turned on by remote.** Should the browser still refuse the sound
   after Play (a policy, a browser that wants its press on the video itself), the film plays muted as
   now, and its "turn the sound on" prompt shows over the film and is answered by a key press, OK
   among them, as well as by a click or a tap.

**Proven by:**
- 1: web/apps/web/src/cast-asked.test.tsx, web/apps/web/src/cast-to.test.tsx, TestCast_ADeclinedOrUnansweredCastTellsItsSenderWhy (the film's name it asks with), VQ76
- 2: web/apps/web/src/cast-asked.test.tsx, web/apps/web/src/cast-receiver.test.tsx, TestHub_LogsThePagesActivationAndThePressThatAnswered, VQ76
- 3: web/apps/web/src/cast-to.test.tsx, TestCast_ADeclinedOrUnansweredCastTellsItsSenderWhy
- 4: web/apps/web/src/cast-asked.test.tsx, web/apps/web/src/cast-to.test.tsx
- 5: web/apps/web/src/cast-receiver.test.tsx, VQ76

> **Revised by [D364](#d364--casting-is-a-session-with-a-device-while-it-lasts-whatever-the-person-plays-plays-there-and-the-sending-device-shows-it-in-the-tray)** (2026-10-27): the receiver is asked once per session, "‹Device› wants to use this device for playback", Use and Not now.

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-27. Built 2026-10-27: the question and its answers (`cast-asked.tsx`,
`live.tsx`), the sender waiting for them (`cast-to.tsx`), the receiver's sound at any press and
its notes (`cast-receiver.tsx`), the film's name in the receive message and the `declined` and
`unanswered` ends (`internal/core/live`, `internal/core/api/casts.go`), and the notes' log lines
(`internal/core/together`). Device checks: VQ76.

## D359 — A library's folder is any folder beneath one of its node's configured roots, chosen by browsing the node's folders

**Decided** (2026-10-27), by the project owner: "The admin should be able to choose any subdir of any
passed-in root for a library root." Until now a library's folders were a node's configured roots
whole (`node.root_paths`), so a node configured with `/tank/media` offered one library over all of
it. The owner's further answers: hidden folders are left out of the browsing ("if anyone starts
asking for it, we can make it an option"), and the same picker serves a new library and changing an
existing one's folders ("do both"). **Keeps**
[D107](#d107--the-node-channel-is-mutually-authenticated-and-a-nodes-roots-are-local-and-never-remotely-settable):
a folder narrows a configured root and never widens it, the node's configuration still the only
place its scope is set; and
[D193 §1](#d193--the-audits-proposals-are-accepted-the-node-does-all-media-work-prepare-is-the-one-path-besides-direct-play-the-machinery-is-cut-and-cut-as-design-freezes):
the node lists the folders, the core opening none.

1. **A library folder is a configured root, or a folder beneath one, named by a clean path and its
   real one.** The core refuses any path its node's hello does not hold, by its text: one with a
   `..`, a `.`, or a doubled or trailing separator is held by none, so no text climbs out of a root
   (`pathtree.DeepestHolding`). The node refuses, at every listing and examining, a folder whose path
   passes through a link or names what is not a directory, and opens the folder as a root of its own
   through `os.Root`, so nothing outside it is read; a link inside the folder is followed as one in a
   root is ([D206](#d206--a-symlink-is-followed-only-into-a-media-root-golangorgxtext-normalises-filenames-and-language-tags)).
   A folder reached through a link is not refused for being elsewhere but for not being its real
   path: the folder itself is offered at its real path. No library's folder may be at, above or below
   another library folder on the same node (one file, one library, one scan); a new library's folders
   may not hold one another either. Each refusal is logged at warn.
2. **The node lists a folder's folders, for an admin, within a time limit.** `GET
   /nodes/{name}/folders?path=` (admin only) asks the node, on its byte socket, for the folders in one
   of its roots or a folder beneath one: no link, even to a folder, and no hidden folder (a name
   starting with "."). The node reads outside every queue and through its disk gate, within the
   window a file's open has, asks of a folder while one listing of it runs sharing it, as probes do
   ([D327](#d327--whoever-needs-to-know-whether-a-root-can-be-read-asks-and-the-node-answers-at-once-outside-every-queue));
   the core waits five seconds at most. A share gone away (`WhenGone: may_wait_forever`) answers
   "this folder is not responding", never hanging the page, the node's channel or its other work.
   Each listing is logged at debug with its node, path, folder count and time; a refused path at
   warn.
3. **One picker chooses a new library's folders and changes an existing library's.** The admin picks
   one of a connected node's configured roots and browses beneath it, never above the root it began
   at. A new library ticks the configured roots or the folders chosen beneath them. An existing
   library adds a folder (`POST /libraries/{id}/roots`, `{nodeName, path}`: the smallest mechanism,
   none existing: the folder is checked as a new library's are, recorded, and scanned at once, as a
   person's request), says one moved to a folder chosen by the same picker (`POST
   /libraries/{id}/roots/repoint`, D241 §6, the folder it moves from covering nothing once moved), and
   retires one (`POST /libraries/{id}/roots/retire`, D231 §7). An added folder may be on any connected
   node.
4. **A folder beneath a configured root is valid wherever a configured root was.** Its scan lists and
   examines it as a root of its own, its scan beginning at its path; a run of chunks, a read-through
   and an extraction read a file named under it; its node's hello asks for its scan when it names the
   root holding it, and one no longer naming that root makes it unavailable
   ([D241 §2](#d241--what-goes-missing-stays-listed-as-unavailable-until-an-admin-says-it-is-gone-and-a-play-of-it-fails-at-once));
   a status saying the root's disk is not answering makes it unavailable, and one saying the disk
   answers again asks for its scan, which brings it back; the watcher's notice under the root scans
   the library folders it touches, the folder changed inside a library's or the library's whole folder
   inside the one changed; the root's watch is shown as its; the node's disk gate keys its readings
   by the root, so one stuck share holds one stuck reading. A library whose folders were the
   configured roots keeps working when the configured roots become their parents: staging's config
   moves from `/tank/media/video/movies`, `/tank/media/video/shows` and
   `/home/yoloai/synctest/movies` to `/tank/media` and `/home/yoloai/synctest`. Landlock is
   unchanged: a confined run is granted its own film, which is under a root either way.
5. **The node protocol is 48:** the byte socket's folder listing (`FolderListing`), and a library
   folder beneath a root named as a command's root, which a node of 47 refuses.

**Proven by:**
- 1: TestDeepestHolding_IsTheDeepestDirectoryHoldingACleanPathAndNoneForAnother, TestAdmin_ALibraryFolderIsAConfiguredRootOrAFolderInsideOneByACleanPath, TestAdmin_LibrariesMayOverlapAndWithinOneAFolderBeneathAnotherAddsNothing (as D363 amended it: libraries may overlap), TestMediaRoot_AFolderIsARootOfItsOwnReachedWithoutALink, TestHolding_IsTheConfiguredRootAFolderIsAtOrUnderByAPathThatCannotClimbOut, TestAgent_RefusesALibraryFolderReachedThroughALinkOrClimbingOutOfItsRoot
- 2: TestServeFolders_ListsTheRealFoldersInAFolderInsideARootAndNothingOutside, TestServeFolders_AShareThatHasGoneIsNotAnsweringWithinTheWindow, TestMediaRoot_SubfoldersAreTheRealFoldersButTheHiddenOnes, TestListFolders_AsksTheNodesByteSocket, TestAdmin_ListsANodesFoldersInsideItsRootsWithinTheWait, TestLibraries_AnAdminBrowsesTheFoldersInsideANodesRoots, web/apps/web/src/folder-picker.test.tsx
- 3: TestLibraries_AnAdminAddsAFolderInsideANodesRootToALibrary, TestRepointRoot_MovesAFolderToAFolderInsideAConfiguredRoot, web/apps/web/src/folder-picker.test.tsx
- 4: TestAgent_ListsAndExaminesALibraryFolderInsideARootReachedWithoutALink, TestAgent_ReadsThroughAVideoNamedUnderALibraryFolderInsideARoot, TestServeFile_ServesAFileUnderALibraryFolderInsideARootAndNothingOutsideIt, TestHello_TheLibraryFoldersInsideARootItNamesAreItsAsTheRootsOwnWere, TestScanSchedule_AWatchersNoticeUnderARootScansTheLibraryFoldersInsideItThatItTouches, TestAdmin_AFolderInsideAConfiguredRootIsListedWithItsOwnWatch
- 5: TestProtocolVersion_IsRaisedWithAnyChangeToTheWire

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-27. Built 2026-10-27: the folder rule in
`internal/platform/pathtree` and `internal/core/library/libraryfolders.go`, the node's folder as a
root of its own and its listing in `internal/node/confine` and `internal/node/byteserver/folders.go`,
the API in `internal/core/api/library_folders.go`, the hello, status and watcher's answers in
`internal/core/nodes` and `internal/core/library/schedule.go`, and the picker in
`web/apps/web/src/folder-picker.tsx`. Staging's roots move to their parents at its next deploy.

**Amended 2026-10-27: the node watches its library folders, never its whole configured roots.** On
staging, once its configured roots became `/tank/media` and `/home/yoloai/synctest`, the node's
watcher, which watched its configured roots, walked and watched the whole of `/tank/media` (audio,
books, photos) over a slow share: five minutes after the start it held some 7,500 watches and was
still adding, and every library said "the watcher has not started" the whole time. Before D359 the
configured roots were the library folders, so the watcher watched only them. What holds now:
1. **The core names the folders the node watches,** in the hello's reply and in each poll's answer
   (`WatchFolders`): each live folder on the node of a live library that watches for changes, and
   nothing else. A library made, deleted or set to watch or not, and a folder added, moved or
   retired, answers the node's waiting poll at once, or its next when none waits, so the change is
   watched within a poll's round trip, not its hold. Nil from a core that names none leaves the
   node's last; empty watches nothing.
2. **The node watches exactly those folders,** starting a folder's watches when it is named and
   releasing them when it no longer is, and refuses one no configured root holds (D107). A folder of a
   configured root that no library uses is never walked or watched; the folder picker's listing
   watches nothing. Each start and stop is logged at info with the folder's count of watches.
3. **Each library folder's watch is its own** in the status and on the Libraries page: not started,
   watching, on a network filesystem, unreadable or at the watch limit, per folder, never the
   configured root's (this replaces §4's "the root's watch is shown as its"). D272 §9's quiet spell
   and its notices are unchanged, per folder.
4. **The node protocol is 49:** `WatchFolders` in the hello's reply and the poll's answer.

**Proven by** (the amendment):
- 1: TestScanSchedule_ANodeWatchesTheFoldersOfItsWatchedLibrariesAndEachChangeIsSaid, TestHelloAndCommands_NameTheFoldersTheNodeWatchesAtOnceWhenTheyChange, TestAgent_HasTheWatcherWatchTheLibraryFoldersTheCoreNames
- 2: TestKernel_WatchesOnlyTheLibraryFoldersItIsGivenNeverTheRestOfTheirRoot, TestKernel_AFolderGivenIsWatchedAndOneNoLongerGivenIsNot, TestKernel_AFolderNoConfiguredRootHoldsIsNotWatchedAndSaysWhy
- 3: TestWatcher_SaysEachLibraryFoldersWatchAndOnlyTheFoldersItIsGiven, TestAdmin_AFolderInsideAConfiguredRootIsListedWithItsOwnWatch, TestWatcher_NoticesTheFolderHoldingARootsChangesOnceItGoesQuiet
- 4: TestProtocolVersion_IsRaisedWithAnyChangeToTheWire

## D360 — The extensions a scan reads are the code's, each container proven to play, and RealMedia is one

**Decided** (2026-10-27), by the project owner: "I also want the ability to view .rm files." Asked
whether the extension lists should stay settings, the owner agreed they should not: which
containers FFmpeg reads is nothing an admin can judge, and as a setting an install keeps the list it
stored, so a container added later never reaches it (a starting value changed reaches only an
unmodified row, D201, and an admin who once edited the list keeps theirs for good). **Amends**
[D240 §8](#d240--the-core-keeps-the-smarts-a-scan-is-a-listing-the-core-compares-the-work-it-implies-is-the-cores-to-schedule-and-the-node-enforces-its-devices-limits-and-pauses-background-work-for-play)'s
"the extension lists are settings": they stay the core's, as a skip rule, but in its code.

1. **The video and subtitle extensions are constants** (`internal/core/library/extensions.go`), not
   the settings `scan_video_extensions` and `scan_subtitle_extensions`. Both keys are retired
   (D202): a stored row is left in place, read by nothing, and listed as unused with why, until a
   person deletes it. The subtitle extensions are those the node converts (D217 §6): `srt`, `ass`,
   `ssa`, `vtt`.
2. **RealMedia is read: `rm` and `rmvb`.** The pinned FFmpeg (8.1.2 with fdproxy, D330) demuxes it
   and decodes RealVideo 1.0 to 4.0 (and 6.0) and RealAudio (Cook, SIPR, ATRAC3, RealAudio
   Lossless, 14.4 and 28.8). None is on the menu (D21), so a RealMedia film is encoded on its
   ladder, picture and sound, for its container, its picture and its sound (D344). Nothing else
   needed changing: the decision's table already converted what it cannot place; the node probes,
   hashes (whole, as any container but Matroska and MP4, D116), reads through for its keyframes
   and cuts its chunks by FFmpeg, whatever the container. RealVideo's sparse keyframes are cut at
   as they come: a film with one every four seconds has four-second chunks.

3. **Every container people kept films in that the pinned FFmpeg can write a film in is read,** each
   proven by a film written in it, in codecs typical of it (the owner: "We should just add all of
   the video types we can at this point (verifying that they work). Beta users will likely have
   collections spanning decades."): Windows Media's `asf`, Media Center's `dvr-ms` (ASF) and `wtv`;
   `ogm`, `mxf`, `dv`, `nut`, `ivf`, `y4m` and `xvid` (an AVI); MP4's relatives `f4v`, `3g2` and
   `qt`, and Matroska's 3D `mk3d`; MPEG program streams `mpe`, `m2p`, DVD-VR's `vro` and HD DVD's
   `evo`; and transport streams `trp`, `tp`, `m2t` and the camcorders' `tod`. Each is decided as its
   codecs need, played as it is (`mk3d` with H.264 and AAC), its picture copied (`f4v`, `qt`, `trp`)
   or encoded, and its first chunk made. Proving them found that a picture carrying a timecode, as an
   MXF's or a camera's MOV does, had the MP4 muxer add a timecode track to each raw file, which the
   node refused; the node now tells the muxer to write none.
4. **Left out:**
   - *Also used by what is no film:* `mod` (a camcorder's MPEG program stream, but also a tracker's
     music), `m4p` (iTunes' protected sound, not video), `ps` (PostScript), `dat` (a VCD's MPEG, but
     any data), `swf` (Flash's animations and programs), `ogg` (Ogg's sound; its video is `ogv`),
     `asx` (a playlist).
   - *Written by FFmpeg, but proven not to play:* `m2v` and `m1v`, elementary MPEG video, which
     carry no container's timing, so the probe has no length and the film cannot be cut; and `amv`,
     whose films FFmpeg's muxer writes without a length, so whether a real player's file plays waits
     for a real sample.
   - *Read by FFmpeg but not written, awaiting a real sample* (the owner will find test films; each
     is added once one plays): Nullsoft's `nsv`, MythTV's `nuv`, TiVo's `ty`, RED's `r3d`, Bink's
     `bik`, Smacker's `smk`, CCTV recorders' `dav` and `ifv`, and `vivo`.

**Proven by:**
- 1: TestReadRules_ReadTheOlderContainersByDefault (a stored row of either retired key changes
  nothing), TestRetiredKeys_AreNotInUseAndSayWhen
- 2: TestPlayback_EachContainerAddedIsReadProbedDecidedAndItsFirstChunkMade (integration tier:
  a RealVideo 2.0 film and a RealVideo 1.0 one, each with RealAudio 14.4, as the pinned FFmpeg writes
  them, are read as videos, probed, decided onto their ladders for container, picture and sound,
  and their first chunks made),
  TestDecide_ARealMediaFilmIsEncodedOnItsLadder, TestDecide_SortsEachVideoStreamIntoOneMenuEntry,
  TestDecide_SortsEachAudioStreamIntoOneMenuEntry
- 3: TestPlayback_EachContainerAddedIsReadProbedDecidedAndItsFirstChunkMade (integration tier,
  a film of each), TestArguments_WriteNoTimecodeTrackBesideTheStream
- 4: TestReadRules_ReadNoExtensionOfWhatIsNoFilmOrIsUnproven

## D361 — The admin's libraries are a list, each library managed on a page of its own, creating one is a page too, and the folder browser is a modal dialog

**Decided** (2026-10-27), by the project owner: "The library management page is a bit ugly. Let's
make it so that there's a list of libraries with basic info about them, and a button 'manage this
library'. Also, the 'create a library' should be its own page, and the folder browser should be a
modal rather than drawing on the page itself." And: "I want the ability to delete libraries", plainly
on the page that manages one. Until now one page held every library's whole card, every action of
each, and the new-library form beneath them, and the folder browser
([D359](#d359--a-librarys-folder-is-any-folder-beneath-one-of-its-nodes-configured-roots-chosen-by-browsing-the-nodes-folders))
drew itself into the page wherever it was opened. **Keeps** every action and its confirmation
([D231 §7](#d231--work-is-derived-from-state-the-job-queue-is-a-regenerable-cache-and-a-destination-that-is-down-parks-its-work),
[D241 §6](#d241--what-goes-missing-stays-listed-as-unavailable-until-an-admin-says-it-is-gone-and-a-play-of-it-fails-at-once),
[D357](#d357--a-rescan-re-runs-the-matcher-on-everything-a-person-did-not-set-per-item-per-library-and-for-all-of-them),
D359 §3); only where each is changes.

1. **`/libraries` lists the libraries at a glance.** Each is a card of its name, what it holds, how
   many folders it reads, how it notices changes and whether a scan runs now, its folders each with
   the warning sign of one with a problem, its files by filing, a rescan running, and "Manage this
   library". The page offers "Create a library", leading to its own page, and "Rescan everything"
   (D357 §1). Nothing that changes one library is on the list.
2. **`/libraries/<id>` manages one library.** Back to the list; its name and the same glance; its
   folders with their state, the answers about a gone root or disk, saying one moved, retiring one and
   adding one; how it notices changes; its files by filing and the link to what the scanner saw; its
   scan and its rescan (D357); the note of what was last asked; and deleting it, confirmed first, after
   which the list shows. An address no library has says so.
3. **The folder browser is a modal dialog**, opened by a button wherever a folder is chosen: creating a
   library, adding a folder, saying one moved. It is a `ModalDialog`, the app's one way to show a
   dialog: the page behind it darkened and taking no press, focus held inside it. It lists the node's
   roots and the folders beneath them as D359 §2 does, "not responding" with Try again included;
   choosing a folder closes it and hands the folder back; Cancel, Escape or a remote's Back close it
   with nothing chosen. As every `ModalDialog` now does, it gives focus back to what had it once it
   closes: the browser does not for a dialog the page removes (idiosyncrasies.md).
4. **`/libraries/new` creates a library**, the form as it was; once made, the new library's page takes
   the form's place in the history, so Back from it returns to the list.
5. **Each page is a route the router knows**, so a deep link, a reload and Back reach it.

## D362 — A video that nothing gives a picture gets a still of its own frames, the last resort once every other source was tried, and the tiles in view raise its making

**Decided** (2026-10-27), by the project owner: an other video's tile had a picture only from an
image beside it or an NFO, and nothing took one from the video. *"Generated screenshots should only
be made available as a last resort for films and series, and get overridden as soon as a real poster
becomes available. Probably best to show using the same poster layout as the rest, with the
screenshot in the top half of the poster space, and the 'no poster' logo lower down so that it's
visible."* And: *"What I mean by last resort is that we've already tried all other methods. I don't
want it pre-emptively generating screenshots just because IMDB hasn't been queried yet."* And:
*"viewing a library signals interest in what's needed to display the tiles with images."* **Extends**
[D212](#d212--artwork-every-image-re-encoded-by-the-node-a-webp-base-kept-by-the-core-nine-sizes-jpeg-cut-by-the-core-and-a-ceiling-that-evicts-what-can-be-remade)
with a source of its own, and
[D324](#d324--work-follows-interest-what-is-played-comes-first-then-what-is-being-looked-at-then-everything-else-work-in-the-way-is-stopped-and-what-waits-says-how-long)
§1's looks with a list's tiles; **amends**
[D349](#d349--libraries-are-browsed-on-a-page-of-their-own-which-replaces-search-a-kind-other-holds-the-videos-that-are-never-identified-films-and-series-gather-every-library-of-theirs-but-those-a-person-leaves-out)
§3's 16:9 tile, which a frame still fills last.

1. **The node takes the still, and re-encodes it as any image.** It reads the video as every run
   reads its film ([D330](#d330--ffmpeg-reads-its-input-through-the-node-over-a-protocol-of-our-own-patched-into-jellyfin-ffmpeg),
   by the fdproxy protocol alone, or the file protocol alone where its FFmpeg lacks it), once it is
   the file the core named (D100), from a tenth of its length, for at most 20 seconds: every picture
   at least 95% black (luma 32 or under, blackframe's own threshold) is dropped, and FFmpeg's
   `thumbnail` filter chooses the most representative of the next 100, so a fade or a black lead-in is
   never the still. The frame, its pixels made square and at most 3840 a side, is one PNG of FFmpeg's
   own with none of the video's metadata; the node hashes it, and re-encodes it as it does any image
   (D212): our WebP, at the landscape sizes it is large enough for, cropped to 16:9. A size larger
   than the base it made is not taken again: the frame is all there is of it. The node protocol is
   version 50.
2. **It is the last resort, and real artwork always wins.** A still is planned for a film with no
   poster and no backdrop, an episode with no still, and an other video with neither, and only once
   every other source was tried and gave none: its library reads NFO files alone, or it follows no
   source (its search found nothing) or its NFO, or its source's answer is stored, and for an episode,
   its series' answer and its season's listing; never while it awaits its match, is ambiguous (a
   person's choice is owed), its fetch failed, or an image a source names of its kinds is still to
   come: not yet fetched, or missing at its source and not yet looked at again
   ([D213](#d213--a-good-netizen-a-dead-image-is-checked-once-more-refresh-rolls-per-provider-and-nothing-is-deleted-because-a-provider-dropped-it)
   §1). An image refused for good was tried. An other video is never matched, and its pass has read
   what is beside it. The job looks again before it runs, and takes no still where the item has come
   to show a picture of its kind. The still is kept as the item's still, its source `frame`, and any
   other image of a kind outranks it in what is shown, at the next read of the page, with no step of
   anyone's. What shows:
   - an other video keeps D349 §3's 16:9 tile: its still, else its backdrop, else its frame still;
   - an episode's frame still is its still, where it has none of its own;
   - a film or series with no poster keeps the 2:3 poster tile of every other: its still fills the
     top half, the mark of a missing poster (the clapperboard and "No poster") below it. The still is
     its backdrop, else a film's frame still, else, for a series, its first episode's still: the first
     of its first regular season in its aired ordering, else of its specials, which a frame of that
     episode gives where nothing else does. A series needs no still of its own.
3. **Stills are made in the background.** Each pass over a library (a scan's, and the sweep's that
   identifies every library again) queues a `make_artwork_sizes` job for each video it finds owed one,
   at the background's priority, which runs in the node's artwork slot as every re-encode does, where
   anything a person waits for, and every play, comes first (D324 §4).
4. **The tiles in view raise their pictures' work, as a page looked at raises its own.** Every grid of
   tiles, a library's, Films', Series', a folder's videos, says the items whose tiles are in view
   (`PUT /tiles/interest`) once they settle for half a second, again every
   interest_said_every_seconds while the tab is visible, and that it shows none when it goes
   (`DELETE`), of the items its person reaches. The interest register keeps each session's tiles as a
   look of its own beside its page, since the list was first shown however far it scrolls, and the
   raiser raises it as it raises a page's: at a look's priority, the latest look first, its tiles
   scrolled away from released. It raises the work of the items, their artwork's, and asks for no
   file's read.
5. **Each still is logged, and a video with no frame is kept so.** The node logs each still taken,
   with its job, its video, where in it and how long it took, and each failure with why; the core logs
   each still kept with its item. A video whose stretch is black throughout, or that has no picture
   at all (which the core knows from its probe and never sends), is recorded as having no frame, and is
   not asked again until the video changes, its size or its time. A still that failed is asked again
   once a scan has seen its video since, as an image beside the media is (G9).

**Proven by:**
- 1: TestStill_FFmpegReadsOnlyTheFilmFromItsPlaceAndSkipsTheBlack, TestStill_AVideosStillSkipsItsBlackLeadInAndBecomesOurOwnWebP, TestAgent_TakesAStillFromTheVideoTheCoreNamedAndReEncodesIt, TestHandle_AFrameStillIsTakenFromTheVideoAndKeptAsTheItemsStill
- 2: TestTake_AFilmGetsAFrameStillOnlyOnceEverySourceWasTriedAndGaveNoPicture, TestTake_AnEpisodeAndAnOtherVideoGetAFrameStillWhenNothingElseShowsThem, TestFoundImages_HandsTheArtworkServiceEveryImageAPassFound, TestHandle_AFrameStillIsTakenFromTheVideoAndKeptAsTheItemsStill, TestHandle_AVideoWithNoFrameIsHeldSoAndAPictureShownTakesNone, TestWithLandscapes_AFrameStillShowsOnlyWhereNoOtherPictureIs, TestWithPosters_APosterlessFilmOrSeriesShowsAStillUntilAPosterArrives, TestEntryBody_SaysEveryPictureTheEntryShows, web/apps/web/src/poster.test.tsx, web/apps/web/src/browse.test.tsx
- 3: TestTake_AFilmGetsAFrameStillOnlyOnceEverySourceWasTriedAndGaveNoPicture
- 4: TestRegister_ASessionsTilesInViewAreALookBesideItsPage, TestRaiser_TilesInViewRaiseTheirItemsWork, TestInterest_ASessionSaysTheTilesItShowsAndLeavesThem, TestReach_AnEditorReachesOnlyTheLibrariesTheirRoleLists, web/apps/web/src/tile-interest.test.tsx
- 5: TestTake_AFrameStillIsNotAskedAgainButAFailureIsOnceAScanSeesTheVideo, TestStill_NothingWrittenIsAVideoWithNoFrame, TestHandle_AVideoWithNoFrameIsHeldSoAndAPictureShownTakesNone, TestAgent_TakesAStillFromTheVideoTheCoreNamedAndReEncodesIt

## D363 — Libraries may overlap: a file is found once, at every place it is, and each list shows an item once however a person reaches it

**Decided** (2026-10-27), by the project owner: "Overlap between libraries should be allowed", the
model agreed point by point the same day, and of copies and folders within folders: "If I happen to
add two directories to a library, and they have some duplicates (or perhaps one directory is a parent
of the other), I don't want it to show me duplicate entries. Same goes for when I'm in the libraries
page, viewing 'All libraries'"; "We'd have to be careful of edge cases like an item that has a
duplicate, but the current user only has access to one of those duplicates via his library access";
and "I don't want to try to handle the case of different encodes of the same video. Let them show up
as duplicates, and the admin can handle it at the filesystem level." Until now a file belonged to one
library (`file.library_id`), so a folder could be in one library alone:
[D359 §1](#d359--a-librarys-folder-is-any-folder-beneath-one-of-its-nodes-configured-roots-chosen-by-browsing-the-nodes-folders)
refused a folder at, above or below another library's, and a copy of a file at a second path was a
second file, shown twice
([D179](#d179--a-files-identity-is-a-hash-of-its-media-payload-not-its-bytes-a-rebuild-restores-the-identity-rows-and-runs-an-ordinary-scan-duplicates-are-surfaced)).
**Revises** D359 §1 (its refusal of overlap) and D179 (a copy at a second path); **removes** the
`mixed` kind of library (D349), which no library has.

1. **Libraries may overlap.** A library's folder may be at, above or below another library's, on any
   node. Within one library, a folder beneath another of its folders adds nothing: adding one is
   refused as already covered, and adding a parent takes its children's place.
2. **The file is the base unit, found at one or more places.** A place is a node and a path. Each place
   is scanned and watched once, whatever libraries cover it. A file's identity stays its payload hash
   (D179); a file at a second place whose hash matches a live file elsewhere is a candidate copy, and
   becomes the same file only once a full read of both shows the same bytes (D116's whole-file pass,
   run for that pair alone). Until then, and if they differ, they are two files; a difference is
   logged.
3. **What lies beside a file is the place's.** Subtitles, images and NFO files beside a copy belong to
   that place; a person is offered those of the places they reach.
4. **A library covers places; it does not own files.** A file is in every library that covers one of
   its places. Nothing records a file's library; coverage is the libraries' folders.
5. **A file is part of at most one film, one run of episodes and one other video.** Libraries of the
   same kind covering it share that one item. Libraries of different kinds covering it each give it
   the item of their kind: a film library and an other library over one folder show the film and the
   other video. A film's different files, a re-encode or a 4K copy, stay its versions (D155).
6. **Each list shows an item once, however it is reached.** A library's list, All libraries, Films,
   Series, Home and a folder's videos list items, never files or places: an item two folders, two
   libraries or two copies reach appears once.
7. **Different files of one other video stay separate.** Two encodes of a home video are two items;
   nothing guesses that they are one, and the admin settles it on disk.
8. **A person reaches only the places their libraries cover, and learns of no other.** They see an item
   when any of its files has a place they reach; they play only from places they reach, and fall back
   to another of those only, when a disk stops answering; nothing they are shown names or counts a
   place they cannot reach. An admin sees every place of a file, and the doctor lists the files found
   at more than one place.
9. **An item's match, where its sources disagree:** a person's match wins (D357); else the NFO beside
   the place first found; the doctor lists the items whose places' NFO files disagree.
10. **Deleting a library deletes no item.** What no library covers any more is kept, its data
    reapable: reaped only under storage pressure, by the existing budgets, oldest first. A person's
    progress stays with the file, and a library covering it again finds it as it was.
11. **Items stay members of collections** ([D160](#d160--there-is-no-series-concept-a-sequence-is-what-a-collection-produces-and-next-up-is-a-query-over-any-of-them)),
    whatever libraries cover them.
12. **The migration carries production's database** (nas.example's, at step 0059) to the new model: each
    file's library becomes a coverage of its place, and nothing a person did is lost.

**Proven by:**
- 1: TestAdmin_LibrariesMayOverlapAndWithinOneAFolderBeneathAnotherAddsNothing, TestLibraries_AnAdminAddsAFolderInsideANodesRootToALibrary, TestScanRootOf_IsTheOutermostFolderAtOrAboveWithTheScopeWithinIt; VQ80
- 2: TestScans_AFolderInsideAnotherLibrarysFolderIsScannedOnceWithinIt, TestScans_AnAskForAnInnerFolderIsItsScopeWithinTheOuter, TestScanSchedule_ANodeWatchesAFolderInsideAnotherOnlyThroughIt, TestCopies_AFileFoundAtASecondPlaceWithTheSameBytesIsOneFileAtTwoPlaces, TestCopies_AFileWithTheSamePayloadAndOtherBytesStaysAFileOfItsOwn, TestRemovePlace_AFilesFirstPlaceGoingLeavesItAtItsCopysPlace, TestAgent_ReadsAFileWholeForTheHashOfItsEveryByte, TestRunners_EveryKindsWorkIsDerivedByASweepOrAskedForByAPlayAndItsOwnFailureIsAFact; VQ81

## D364 — Casting is a session with a device: while it lasts, whatever the person plays plays there, and the sending device shows it in the tray

> **Revised by [D371](#d371--a-session-has-a-leader-that-plays-as-a-device-plays-alone-everyone-else-catches-up-to-it-and-a-cast-takes-its-senders-part)** (2026-10-28): the receiver leads the cast's session and plays each film as the device plays one alone, nothing steering it; the remote's commands are carried out by the receiver as its own press, and the receiver's state, with how it plays (delivery, quality, link), comes back for the remote to show.

**Decided** (2026-10-27), by the project owner: "Rather than make it only for the current video, let's
make it start a control session with the device. While this session is active, any video I play gets
played on that device. This would end up behaving somewhat similarly to the watch together session.
We should also have an icon in the status tray while casting is active so that they know. If the
device takes back control, it behaves as now: continue with the currently playing video. If no video
is playing, go back to the home screen." The owner then answered the open questions the same day: the
receiver stays full screen between videos; a session is set up only from a top-bar item "Cast", as
Watch Together is, and the receiver asks "‹Device› wants to use this device for playback"; Play goes
to the receiver, the remote offering to play on this device instead; a session lasts until it is
stopped or its receiver is gone; the receiver asks once; the tray icon is the sending device's alone.
Until now a cast carried one film
([D337](#d337--casting-starts-with-a-persons-own-signed-in-devices-one-chosen-from-those-connected-now-plays-the-film-the-one-that-cast-becomes-its-remote-and-either-may-take-control-back)),
its receiver returning to its page when it ended
([D338](#d338--a-cast-goes-to-the-devices-tab-in-front-its-receiver-keeps-a-televisions-controls-and-leaves-by-back-or-a-double-ok-and-stop-casting-returns-it-to-the-page-it-was-on)),
and each cast asked the receiver first
([D358](#d358--a-cast-asks-the-receiving-device-first-device-wants-to-play-film-here-whose-play-is-the-press-that-starts-it-with-sound-and-full-screen)).
**Revises** D337 (a cast is a session, not a film), D338 (where the receiver goes) and D358 (one
question per session); **keeps** D337 §1, §5's remote and split devices, §6 (the last cast wins) and
§7 (the receiver's own controls), and D88 (casting is Watch Together with a group of one).

1. **A session is started from the top bar's "Cast",** as Watch Together is: it lists the person's
   other devices connected now (D337 §2), and choosing one starts the session. The Play page no
   longer offers to cast. A video playing on the sending device when the session starts moves to the
   receiver at its position.
2. **The receiver asks once:** "‹Device› wants to use this device for playback", Use and Not now,
   unanswered after a minute as D358 has it. Use is the press that turns the sound on and goes full
   screen (D358 §2).
3. **While the session lasts, whatever the person plays on the sending device plays on the
   receiver:** a film, an episode, Resume, Next Up, the next episode played on by itself. The sending
   device's Play page is the receiver's remote (D337 §5), and the person browses on it freely.
4. **The remote offers "Play on this device instead"** for the video at hand: it plays there from the
   receiver's position, and the session goes on for the next.
5. **Between videos the receiver stays full screen** on a quiet "Ready, controlled from ‹Device›"
   page, so the next video starts full screen and with sound, with no press on it.
6. **The session lives in the core, not in the sending tab.** A sending device that sleeps, locks or
   reloads finds the session again and shows it; the session ends only by Stop casting, by the
   receiver taking control back, by another cast to the receiver (the last cast wins, D337 §6), or
   when the receiver has been gone for two minutes, which the sending device is told.
7. **The sending device shows a tray icon on every page** while the session lasts, naming the receiver
   and what it plays. The receiver shows none.
8. **The remote is a page of its own the person returns to from anywhere** (the owner: *"I cast to my
   TV, then start Wings playing. I then start browsing to Quillwick … Then I think actually I want to
   continue with wings. Now I need a way to go back to the remote controls for the already playing
   Wings on the TV"*). The tray icon, and the top bar's Cast while a session lasts, lead to it: the
   remote of what plays on the receiver, at its position, with Stop casting; with nothing playing,
   "Ready on ‹Device›", Stop casting and nothing else. Browsing away leaves the video playing on; Back
   from the remote returns to where the person was.
9. **Taking control back on the receiver** (Back, Escape, a double OK or click, D338) ends the session:
   a video playing goes on there as an ordinary player (D338 as the owner kept it); with none playing,
   the receiver goes to its home page.
10. **Stop casting on the sending device** ends the session and returns the receiver to the page it was
    on before the session began (D338 §4); the sending device is offered "Play here from ‹time›" for a
    video that was playing.
11. **With Watch Together also running, one place holds the playback controls** (the owner: *"It could
    become confusing if both icons are up, and both pages they lead to have playback controls. Maybe
    when both features are active, it's best to have the cast page have an 'end casting' button and a
    'go here for playback controls' button that takes them to the watch together page, which has the
    more complete set of controls"*). The cast page then offers End casting and a way to Watch
    Together's page, where the controls are; it shows none of its own. How the two tray icons read
    side by side is designed with the build, and shown to the owner before it is built.

**Revised before it was built** (2026-10-27), by the owner's answers to
[screens-and-guest-rejoin-2026-10-27.md](../design/research/screens-and-guest-rejoin-2026-10-27.md)
§5 ([navigation-and-widgets-answers-2026-10-27.md](../design/plans/navigation-and-widgets-answers-2026-10-27.md)).
These points replace §1's top-bar "Cast", §7's tray icon and §11 where they differ:

12. **No Watch Together or Cast item in the top bar.** Their two icons are always in the tray, white while
    their function is off, blue (perhaps pulsing) while it is on, and they are the entry points.
13. **Where each icon leads, by what is on:**

    | Watch Together | Casting | Watch Together's icon | Cast's icon |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | off | off | the session setup page | the casting setup page, the devices one can cast to |
    | on | off | the session's page | the casting setup page; a cast set up, the session's page |
    | off | on | the session setup page | the casting page: playback controls, End the session |
    | on | on | the session's page, with Stop casting | the session's page |

14. **Watch Together's icon shows for everyone in a session, host or signed-in guest**, not a guest
    who joined by a link alone; a signed-in guest browses freely and returns by it.
15. **Leaving the film no longer stops it for the group**: Stop, or the host playing another film,
    ends it (D246 §5's stop on leaving is withdrawn). The session's page carries the playback controls (the remote of
    D369's `PlayerControls`).
16. **No mini player and no picture-in-picture** without a very compelling reason.

**Proven by:**
- 1, 12: TestCast_IsASessionOnlyItsReceiverAccepts (started with nothing playing), cast-to.test.tsx ("lists the person's other devices open now, and starts a session with the one chosen, moving the film playing here", "starts a session with nothing playing where no film was playing here"), status-tray.test.tsx ("has Cast's sign on a film's Play page take the film to the casting page"), cast-remote.test.tsx ("lists the devices to cast to when this device casts nothing"), title.test.tsx ("offers no cast of its own"), web/e2e/cast.spec.ts
- 2: TestRegistry_ACastIsASessionTheSenderIsToldOf, TestCast_IsASessionOnlyItsReceiverAccepts, cast-asked.test.tsx ("asks whether to use this device for playback", "asks for the page full screen in Use's own press, tells the server"), cast-to.test.tsx ("asks once whether to be used for playback", "goes full screen and ready between videos, then plays the next with no question"); VQ90

- 16: nothing built: no mini player, no picture-in-picture.

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-27. Built 2026-10-27. The core keeps the session
(`internal/core/live/registry.go`): a cast may start with nothing playing (`fileId` 0, the receiver
ready), `Play` hands the receiver each film the person plays, or nothing, in the same cast, `Accept`
notes its Use, and a new live message, `sending`, tells every page of the sending device the cast it
sends, as a page opens (before its devices, so a Play there knows at once) and at each change and end;
a receiver with no connection for `ReceiverGoneAfter` (two minutes) is ended by `EndGone`, looked at
every ten seconds (`cmd/orpheum/casts_gone.go`), its sender told `receiverGone`. The endpoints
(`internal/core/api/casts.go`): `POST /me/casts` with `fileId` optional, `POST /me/casts/{id}/play`
(a film, or none; none stops the cast's group, `together.Hub.CastReady`, so the next is put on
afresh), `POST /me/casts/{id}/accept`; `filmEnded` is no longer a cast's end. The web client
(`web/apps/web/src/`): the tray's two signs (`status-tray.tsx`), white off, the status blue on with a
slow 3 s breathing of the icon's opacity (1 to 0.55), none where less motion is asked for; the
top bar's Watch Together item gone (`app-shell.tsx`); the casting page (`cast-remote.tsx`, the device
list and the wait for Use in `cast-to.tsx`), the remote of a session's film shared with Watch
Together's page (`session-remote.tsx`, `together-plays.tsx`), `PlayOrSendOn` deciding once by the
live connection, the receiver's question and ready page (`cast-asked.tsx`, `cast-ready.tsx`,
`live.tsx`), the film playing here as the Cast sign is pressed (`playing-here.ts`), and the host's
player sending nothing as it is left (`together-host.tsx`, `use-together.ts`). The wire: the live
socket's new `sending` message and `receive`'s `isAccepted` and `togetherCredential` (no version: the
live socket has none, and its pages are served by the same core); Watch Together's protocol is
unchanged but for the cast's end `receiverGone`.

Resolved in the build, where the decision left it open (say if any should go otherwise):
- **Casting while Watch Together is on** (§11, §13) is plans/cast-to-device.md §7's step 8 in its
  simplest form: the receiver is handed a host's credential for the person's session with each film
  and plays it as their player, so what they play plays for the group, the cast's own session only
  telling it how the cast ends. §7's refinements are not built: the receiver is not told its
  person's voice is live, so does not make room for it, and the upload's last resort may still send
  the receiver away with the voice.
- **The receiver asks again after its page is loaded again**: a reloaded page has no press left to
  play with sound or go full screen, so it asks once more for the session it is handed.
- **Cast's sign is blue from the moment a cast is asked for**, while the receiver is asked, not only
  once it said Use; a Play goes to the receiver only after its Use.
- **The title page's Cast is gone too**, as the Play page's is: the tray's sign is the one entry.
- **The receiver's full screen is the page's**, asked in Use's press, which a player's stage no longer
  races to take (`film-fullscreen.ts`, `askPageFullScreen`); full screen ended as the page removes its
  element is no one taking control back (`cast-receiver.tsx`): the second film of a session had taken
  control back as it opened.
- **A film's end with Up next shown and autoplay off** stays on the offer, as before, rather than
  going to the ready page; the next Play on the sender goes to it all the same.

## D365 — Among a film's candidates, the one whose runtime fits the file is preferred, a year either side of the name's, then the most voted

**Decided** (2026-10-27), by the project owner: "I'm fine with preferring the candidate whose runtime
fits best. We could also look at the popularity of a film as a heuristic." The case: staging's
*Crowd.2022.1080p.WEBRip* (92.1 minutes) was matched to TMDB 1120937, an obscure 2022
*Crowd* of 88 minutes, by
[D301 §1](#d301--an-unsettled-match-takes-the-oldest-candidate-the-most-voted-within-a-year-and-an-admin-corrects-it-from-the-titles-page)'s
"most votes among those of that year"; the film it is, TMDB 1020910 (92 minutes), TMDB dates 2023,
its festival premiere 2022. A rule only passing over a candidate the file's length contradicts could
not tell 88 from 92 minutes, as credits, cuts and PAL speed-up move a film's length by as much.
**Revises** D301 §1 for films; series keep it, an episode's length saying little of its series.

1. **A film's candidates are ranked by how their runtime fits the file's duration**, where the file's
   duration and a candidate's runtime are both known: a candidate **fits** when they differ by at most
   3 minutes or 3% of the runtime, the larger; one whose runtime is unknown neither fits nor
   contradicts; one that differs by more contradicts. Fitting candidates come first, then those of
   unknown runtime, then those that contradict. A fit only orders candidates whose names match (D172's
   tiers); it never makes a match of a name that does not.
2. **A year in the file's name or its NFO admits the candidates of that year and of a year either
   side**, since a premiere and a release, or a release in two countries, fall in different years;
   within one class of fit, the candidate of the named year comes before one a year off. With no year,
   all the name's candidates are admitted.
3. **Within that, the most popular is taken**: the most votes at the source, as D301 §1 has for a year
   given; with no year in the name, the oldest, as D301 §1 has (Disney's *The Thief of Bagdad* over a later one),
   the fit coming first.
4. **The runtimes are fetched once and kept**: a candidate's runtime is read from the source's details
   of it, as the matcher reads the rest, kept with the candidate (cache.db's `match_candidate`), and
   fetched again only when the candidate is.
5. **The choice says why** in the log: each candidate's year, runtime, votes and class of fit, and the
   one taken, so a wrong guess explains itself.

**Proven by:**
- 1: TestMatch_AFilmsCandidateWhoseRuntimeFitsTheFileIsTaken, TestMatch_AFilmsCandidatesAreRankedFitsUnknownThenContradicts
- 2: TestMatch_AFilmsYearAdmitsAYearEitherSideItsOwnFirst, TestMatch_AFilmsCandidateWhoseRuntimeFitsTheFileIsTaken, TestMatch_TheYearIsAStrongerCueThanTheExactName
- 3: TestMatch_AFilmWithNoYearTakesTheOldestOfThoseThatFitBest, TestMatch_SeveralOfOneNameAreSettledByAGuessMarkedAsOne
- 4: TestMatch_AFilmsCandidateWhoseRuntimeFitsTheFileIsTaken, TestRescan_AKeptCandidatesRuntimeIsNotFetchedAgain
- 5: TestMatch_AFilmsChoiceAmongItsCandidatesIsLogged

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-27. Built 2026-10-27: the ranking in
`internal/core/identify/settle_film.go`, the runtimes read, kept and logged in
`internal/core/identify/runtimes.go`, used by the first match (`match.go`) and a rescan's
(`rematch.go`); a file's length from `ListLiveFilesOfTitle`. Several candidates all a year off the
file's, none fitting it, stay a person's choice as D301 §1 had them; runtimes are read only where
several are admitted and a file's length is known, so a film matched before its file is probed is
ranked by year and votes alone.

## D366 — Every sort runs either way, films and series also sort by release date, and each person chooses which libraries fill their Home

**Decided** (2026-10-27), by the project owner: "One more thing I want in the next batch: The ability
to sort by date", then "sorting needs to handle newest to oldest, oldest to newest, a-z, z-a"; and of
Home: "whether a library's items show up on the home page … It's a choice each person makes."
Until now a films or series library sorted by name or by date added, an other library also by
recorded date and file name
([D349 §4](#d349--libraries-are-browsed-on-a-page-of-their-own-which-replaces-search-a-kind-other-holds-the-videos-that-are-never-identified-films-and-series-gather-every-library-of-theirs-but-those-a-person-leaves-out)),
each one way only, and Home drew on every library a person reaches. **Keeps** D349 §2 (the sort is
in the page's address), §8 (a person leaves a library out of Films and Series) and §9 (the alphabet
rail).

1. **Films and series sort by release date too:** a film's release date, a series' first air date,
   as the source gives them, the year alone where no day is known.
2. **Every sort runs either way.** Dates newest to oldest or oldest to newest; names and file names
   A–Z or Z–A. The direction is part of the sort the page's chooser offers and its address keeps
   (D349 §2), each sort with the default direction it has now (dates newest first, names A–Z).
3. **What a sort cannot place goes last, whichever way it runs:** an item with no date at the end of
   a sort by date, newest first or oldest first.
4. **The alphabet rail follows a name sort's direction** (D349 §9): Z–A lists its letters Z to A; a
   date sort shows none.
5. **Each person chooses which libraries fill their Home,** beside D349 §8's choice for Films and
   Series, kept on their account and made on their own settings: every library they reach is on it
   by default; one they leave out adds nothing to any row of Home (Continue Watching, Next Up, the
   newest), and stays on the Libraries page and in Films and Series as §8 has it. An item that two
   libraries reach (D363) shows on Home while any library of the person's that reaches it is left in.

**Proven by:**
- 1: TestPass_AFilmAndASeriesAreDatedByTheirSourcesDayElseTheirYear, TestMatch_AFilmIsDatedByItsProvidersReleaseDate, TestFetchAndParse_AFilmsDetails, TestSeries_FetchParseAndItsSeasons, TestMigrate_Step0061DatesEachTitleAndSeriesByItsYear, TestBrowse_EverySortRunsEitherWayAndWhatHasNoDateIsLast; VQ83
- 2: TestBrowse_EverySortRunsEitherWayAndWhatHasNoDateIsLast, TestBrowse_OtherVideosRunEitherWay, web/apps/web/src/library-browse.test.tsx, alphabet-rail.test.tsx, router.test.ts; VQ83
- 3: TestBrowse_EverySortRunsEitherWayAndWhatHasNoDateIsLast (pages of two across the dated and the undated, both ways)
- 4: TestBrowse_ZToAFromANameStartsAtTheLastTitleBeforeIt, web/apps/web/src/alphabet-rail.test.tsx ("the rail follows a name sort's direction"), library-browse.test.tsx; VQ83
- 5: TestHome_ALibraryLeftOutOfHomeAddsNothingToItsRows, web/apps/web/src/account.test.tsx, home.test.tsx; VQ83

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-27. Built 2026-10-27: the release day in
`internal/store/migrations/0061_films_and_series_are_dated_by_their_release.sql` (`released_on` on
title and collection, YYYYMMDD with 00 for a month or day unknown, indexed per kind), read by the

release_date or first_air_date (`internal/core/providers/tmdb/works.go`); each list's other way in

(`left_out_of_home`) and `internal/core/api/library_browsing.go` (`homeReach`, GET

## D367 — Up goes a level up from any page to its parent, Back goes back the way the person came

**Decided** (2026-10-27), by the project owner: "the general rule is: You can drill down to get to a
playback item, and use 'up' to go back up. Back goes back the way you came, like a browser." It came
from Continue Watching: Back from a film started on Home returns to Home, as it should, but nothing
went a level up for the item; and of where a film goes up to, its own page (the owner's choice of
option 1). Until now the Play page went up only when nothing of the app was behind it (its Back, the
Play page's `playUp`, built the same day) and other pages had Back alone.

1. **Back is the browser's back**: the way the person came, Home after Continue Watching, the list a
   tile was chosen from, as each history step was; a remote's Back the same. Nothing changes it.
2. **Up goes to the page's parent, on every page that has one,** a control of its own beside Back,
   reachable by a remote as any control is:
   - playing an episode → its series at its season (the person's ordering, as the Play page's
     `playUp` has it); a film or an extra → the film's page; an other video → its library's list, at
     its folder where it was browsed by folder;
   - a season → its series; a series' or a film's page → the library it is listed in; an other library's
     folder → the folder above it, its top → the library;
   - a library → Libraries; Libraries, Home, Films, Series and the account's and admin's top pages have
     no parent and show no Up.
3. **The library Up leads to is the one the person came through,** when the page was reached from a
   library; else, for an item two libraries reach (D363), the first of the person's libraries that
   lists it, by name.
4. **Up is a step in the history like any other**, so Back after Up returns to the page Up was pressed
   on.
5. **The Play page's Back with nothing behind it keeps going up** (as built 2026-10-27), to the same
   target as its Up.

**Revised before it was built** (2026-10-27), after the research
([navigation-back-up-2026-10-27.md](../design/research/navigation-back-up-2026-10-27.md)) and the owner's
answers ([navigation-and-widgets-answers-2026-10-27.md](../design/plans/navigation-and-widgets-answers-2026-10-27.md)):
the owner objected that "if you're in a video and click up a bunch, then press back, it brings you back
down again"; no product the research found makes Back go up instead of back. These points replace §2's
"a control of its own beside Back" and §4:

6. **No on-screen Back** on computers and phones: the browser's, the gesture's and the remote's Back is
   the history (§1). A TV keeps an on-screen Back in the player's overlay while the app cannot tell TV
   Bro (whose remote Back never reaches the page) from Silk.
7. **Up never adds to the history.** If the parent is anywhere behind in the app's history, Up goes back
   to the nearest copy of it; otherwise Up replaces the current entry with the parent. Back after Up never
   returns down the branch.
8. **Up shows where one is and leads up**: on computers and phones a trail (`Series › Copper Kettle › S1E1
   Pilot`), each part a link, the one before the last the parent; on a TV one "‹ ‹parent's name›", one
   stop for focus. Top pages show none.
9. **A series is one page with a season picker**; choosing a season, a sort or a search replaces the
   history entry, a view of the page, not a level. Returning to the series, by Back or Up, shows the
   season of the episode one comes back from, that episode focused.
10. **Dialogs close on Back** where the browser lets the page see it (Escape, a remote's Back), before
    the page is left.

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-27. Built 2026-10-27, as revised (§4 replaced by §7, §2's control by §8).
In `web/apps/web/src`: the history keeps, on each entry, the addresses of this app's entries behind it
(`navigation.ts`, `below`), and `navigation.up` goes back to the nearest one showing the parent,
however far (`history.go(-n)`), else puts the parent in the page's place; where each page sits is
`upward.ts` (a library crumb found behind, as the person came through, else the first of the
item's libraries by name; a series', a title's and a film's crumbs; the Play page's in
`play-up.tsx`, the folders' in `library-browse.tsx`'s `folderUpward`); `up-trail.tsx` draws the trail,
each part an Up (`UpLink`), or on a television one "‹ name", and tells a remote's Back the parent
(§5); the television's player overlay (`tv-controls.tsx`) shows Up and the one on-screen Back left
(`back-button.tsx`); a title's, a series', a Play page's, a folder's and the admin's library pages
show the trail in place of their Back; an episode's series and season links are Ups. The series is
one page (`series.tsx`) with a season picker (`route-chooser.tsx`, moved out of
`library-browse.tsx`), its default the season of the person's next episode; a season, a sort, a
view, a search and an episode ordering replace the entry (`link.tsx`'s `isReplacing`; the ordering's
push at `series.tsx` was the duplicate entry the research found); an episode's page and its playing
note the episode reached (`episode-reached.ts`), whose season the series shows, the episode
focused, when returned to; `app.tsx` keys the series' page by the series alone, so a season changes
the view rather than drawing a page anew. The server says where an item sits: a title's and a
series' `libraries` (by name) and an extra's `filmOfExtra` (`internal/core/library/whereabouts.go`,
`internal/core/api/whereabouts.go`), and a playback's `plays` its `libraryName` and `filmOfExtra`.
Silk's base under a page opened directly is kept; its Back goes to the parent of the page shown
(§5). As built, where the decision left it open: a library's list on the Libraries page is a top
page, with no Up (Libraries is the page that lists it); a film's Play page reads "Films › Heat ›
Playing", its last part the playing; Films and Series stand as the list a film or series came
through, as a library's page does; an episode's page goes up to its series, not a season, the
season being a view; the series' picker sits in its head beside the ordering, where a remote's
arrows reach it among the series' other choices (under the episodes' heading, the walk found Play and
the ordering out of the arrows' reach), and lists each season with its episode count and no still.
D370's marks by hand stay: the whole series' in the series' head at every season, the season's
over the season shown, a season watched whole showing its check in the picker. Fixed after the
owner's checks on staging (2026-10-28): a title's backdrop, which rose into the space above it and
whose mask made it a layer of its own, was drawn over the trail's lower half ("the info page banner
covers half of the trail text"); it now starts below the trail (`title.css`). The owner: "When I
play a video, there's no way to go directly back to the info page", then, revising §2's Play page
(2026-10-28): "jellyfin ... always leaves a trail that goes back to the info page before going any
further back. That makes sense, because you go through an info page to get to the playback page in
all cases, including episodes. ... The only exception is direct-play links, such as continue
watching", whose Back goes straight back to the list (§1, as built). So a Play page's parent is
always what plays' own page, an episode's, an extra's, an other video's as a film's: "Series › Ted
Lasso › S1E1 Pilot › Playing", the television's overlay "‹ S1E1 Pilot", and a Back with nothing
behind goes there too (§5); Up from that page goes on to the series at its season, an extra's film,
an other video's library. Each chooser
(`route-chooser.tsx`) shows a down chevron at its button's end and says it opens a dialog
(`aria-haspopup`), the owner: "The choice box UI items look no different from a regular button".
Not seen on a device yet (VQ91).
§10 on a Fire TV, after the owner's check (2026-10-28): "with the chooser widget I can only exit
without choosing by pressing the back button, which actually brings me back a page". Silk's remote
Back is a step of the history, never a key the page hears (idiosyncrasies.md), so a dialog closed
on Escape and a remote's Back key but not there. Every modal dialog, a chooser's list and the menu
among them, now holds an entry of the same address over the page's own while it is open
(`navigation.ts`'s `holdBack`, `modal-dialog.tsx`): the browser's Back steps off it, which closes
the dialog and leaves the page where it was; closed any other way, the dialog takes its entry away
again; a choice that goes, replaces or goes up takes it away first, so the history is what it would
be with nothing open, and Up's search behind (`below`) never meets it. It is done on every browser,
not by feature detection: the page cannot tell a Back that is a key from one that is a step until
it comes, nor TV Bro from Silk (§6), and a phone's Back gesture and a computer's Back button closing
an open dialog first is what those platforms do. One trace is left: the entry a closed list held
stays ahead of the page, as a browser keeps any entry Back left, and Forward onto it steps straight
back off it. Each list also has a Close after its places, which a remote's arrows reach, and Left or
Right closes it, the owner the same day: "We can also make it so that moving left/right while in a
chooser or menu closes it"; the press closes the list alone, focus back on its button, and the next
press moves on from there. The banner's menu, which was a `<details>`, is the chooser's widget
(`drop-down.tsx`'s `DropDown`), the owner: "the menu should share code with it, the only real
difference being that there's no extra visual indicator that it's a dropdown", and "the drop-down
menu should be modal": a press outside it closes it and presses nothing under it, focus stays in it
while it is open, its icon has no chevron. It opens over the page, as a chooser's list does, where
it dropped from its icon before. Not seen on a device yet (VQ97).
§10 revised after the owner's next check on the Fire TV (2026-10-28): "the chooser opening a window
in a different location feels weird. The sort chooser on the films page was missed in the revamp,
but it feels so much nicer on a big screen. Maybe we should do the pop-up version only on small
screens, and try to make them overlap the chooser somehow, so that it's obvious what they belong
to." A drop-down's list now opens at its button (`drop-down-place.ts`): on a big screen, a
television's or a computer's, as a select's list, its current choice laid over the button, the list
as wide as the button at least and scrolled within itself where the screen's edge leaves it no
room; on a phone's (app-shell.css's 599 px breakpoint, `phone-width.ts`), a pop-up whose top is the
button's; either way inside the screen, moved up or across where it must be. The menu opens so at
its icon. It opens on its current choice, never its Close; Left and Right close it from its Close
too; and its opening and closing never move the page, which a list laid out at the page's top had
scrolled (idiosyncrasies.md). The Films and Series pages' sort and a library's files' filing, still
native selects, are choosers of the same drop-down (`route-chooser.tsx`'s `ActionChooser`, the page
keeping the choice); a series' ordering, a preference kept on the server, stays a select for the
owner to decide. Not seen on a device yet (VQ97).
Fixed after the owner's check on the Fire TV (2026-10-29): a series chosen far down the Series list
opened scrolled to its last episodes, the window keeping the list's scroll, and §9's episode reached
