## D368 — On a film's ladder, the top quality plays the film's own sound, copied; the lower qualities keep the light stereo track

**Decided** (2026-10-27), by the project owner. A film played at home in Chrome on the Mac from nas.example,
at the top of its ladder (its own picture, copied), showed its sound as "AAC stereo, 96 kb/s
(transcoded from AAC stereo)": every quality of a film cut into chunks shares one sound track made at
`chunk_sound_kbps`
([D247 §6](#d247--a-slow-link-gets-a-lower-version-made-at-its-first-stall-and-played-from-its-second-and-a-group-waits-for-a-stalled-viewer-once-then-lets-them-catch-up-alone)'s
amendment, set for an airplane's 0.6 Mb/s link), so even a film's own picture plays with a re-encoded
sound, and a 5.1 film is folded down to stereo. That breaks
[D336 §1](#d336--a-films-sound-plays-as-it-is-unless-the-device-cannot-play-it-or-the-person-asks-for-a-feature-that-needs-it-made-no-one-is-asked-how-their-device-makes-sound)'s
"the sound plays as it is by default" on the ladder. The owner agreed the lead's proposal ("yes").
**Revises** D247 §6's amendment (one sound track for every quality).

1. **The top quality, the film's own picture, plays the film's own sound, copied**, every channel,
   wherever the device can play it as it is (D336 §1: its playable formats); a device that cannot
   gets the sound D336 §2 makes for it. The copy is cut at the chunks' boundaries as the picture is.
2. **The lower qualities keep the light stereo track** at `chunk_sound_kbps`, as now: they are for a
   link that cannot carry more.
3. **Each quality names its sound in the master playlist** (an HLS audio group per quality), so the
   player switches sound with picture when it changes quality. Whether that switch is heard (a
   blip) is checked on the owner's devices.
4. **A feature that needs sound made** (the dialogue boost, night mode; D336 §2–§3) plays its made mix at
   every quality, as now.
5. **The play's log line says what was sent:** a chunked play no longer says `delivery=direct`; it
   names the ladder, the quality it started on and the sound it started with.

**Proven by:**
- 1: TestMasterPlaylist_TheTopPlaysTheTracksItsPlayerPlaysAsTheyAreCopied, TestStartOnLadder_StartsTheTopOnTheFilmsOwnSoundCopied, TestStoreFileOf_OffersASoundCopiedOnlyOfATrackTheTopPlaysCopied, TestHandleMakeChunks_ACopiedSoundIsSentAsItsTrackAndAMixAtItsLevelCarriesTheDifference, TestTracks_TheTopNamesTheFilmsOwnSoundItPlaysCopied, TestArguments_CopyASoundAtItsTimesInTheFilmAndCutItAtTheBounds, TestMake_TimesACopiedSoundByItsListedEndInTheFilm, TestMake_ACopiedSoundIsTheFilmsOwnPacketsBitForBitAtTheirTimes (integration tier: 5.1 AAC, stereo AAC and 5.1 AC-3, two runs, the film's packets bit for bit); VQ85
- 2: TestMasterPlaylist_TheTopPlaysTheTracksItsPlayerPlaysAsTheyAreCopied (the lower qualities' group), TestMake_ACopiedSoundIsTheFilmsOwnPacketsBitForBitAtTheirTimes (the light track stereo AAC, none of the film's packets)
- 3: TestMasterPlaylist_EachPictureNamesTheSoundsItPlays, TestMasterPlaylist_TheTopPlaysTheTracksItsPlayerPlaysAsTheyAreCopied, web/packages/player/src/hls.test.ts ("keeping the sound playing as the quality moves between audio groups"); VQ85 (the blip)
- 4: TestMasterPlaylist_TheTopPlaysTheTracksItsPlayerPlaysAsTheyAreCopied (the boosted mix made in the top's group), hls.test.ts ("keeps a rendition chosen, the boosted mix, at every quality"), TestMasterPlaylist_ATrackPlayedCopiedIsMadeAtItsOwnLevelLevellingOrNot; VQ85
- 5: TestPlayback_AChunkedPlayLogsItsLadderTheQualityAndTheSoundItStartsOn, TestPlayback_LogsEachStartAndRefusalButNeverTheToken

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-27. Built 2026-10-27. The node makes a new kind of store, a
sound copied (`nodeproto.StreamSoundCopied`, protocol 53; `internal/node/chunks/arguments.go`,
`maker.go`, `fmp4.go`): copied with `-copyts -start_at_zero`, led in from the chunk before, its first
packet put a tick before the film so the segment muxer, which counts its cuts from a run's first
packet, cuts every run at the same packets, each chunk placed by its listed end less its samples, the
init after the first packet (AC-3); idiosyncrasies.md has both. The core
(`internal/core/chunks/ownsound.go`, `offer.go`, `playlists.go`) offers the top, the picture copied, an audio group of its own,
`own`, holding each track its device plays as it is (`decide.PlaysAsItIs`, kept on the playback as
`ownSoundTracks`) copied, `sound<track>-own`, with its channels, and the rest as the lower qualities'
group `audio` has them; every group in one order, one name to a place. A track played copied has its
mixes made as loud as it, `-ownlevel` (`decide.OwnLevelGainDB`: the stereo mix's levelling less the
track's own), once the film's loudness was measured, levelling or not, so a step between the two keeps
the level and the player levels both by the decision's levelling, as it levels the original played
as it is (D226 §4); a start on such a track carries no gain. Not decided by the owner, chosen to keep
§1 and §3 from a jump in loudness: say if the light track should rather stay levelled (the player
would then need a gain per quality). The player (`keepAudioRendition`, `web/packages/player/src/hls.ts`)
keeps the sound's place as the level moves between groups, where hls.js matches by name and
channels. The start's log line (`internal/core/api/playback.go`) says `delivery=ladder`,
`decidedDelivery`, `ladderQuality` and `ladderSound`. The tracks note
(`web/apps/web/src/tracks-note.tsx`) names the top's own sound from the API's
`pictures[].sounds`. Night mode is not built (D336); the dialogue boost is the made mix at every
quality. A device that cannot play a track's codec and channels gets the light stereo track at the
top too, D336 §2's made sound.

**Revised 2026-10-28** by the owner ("yes", agreeing the lead's fix for the batch): §3's switch
threw the loaded sound away. A Fire TV playing Nosferatu (staging, file 5671, device 60) stepped down
from the top (D352's revision of the same day): hls.js moves the sound to the new quality's group
as it asks for the picture's next chunk, loaded 37 s ahead of where it plays, and, the light
track's channels differing from the copied sound's, flushes all the sound loaded
(`flushAudioIfNeeded`). The sound held 3049.13–3051.62 against the picture's 3049.46–3088.04, the
light track's chunks from there were being made (425), and the TV stalled 1172 ms. **The sound
loaded plays out, and the new quality's sound is loaded on from its end**, so it is heard where
that quality's picture begins: the player switches to the rendition at the place in the form
(channels, codec) of the sound loaded, and gives the rendition its own form back at once
(`keepAudioRendition`, `web/packages/player/src/hls.ts`), which hls.js takes for the same sound and
loads on from the end of the sound loaded, as it does for two groups' stereo tracks of one name; the
init segment the new chunks carry tells the browser their channels and codec, as after a flush. A
sound the person chooses (another track, the dialogue boost) still plays at once, the loaded sound
thrown away. Whether the browser plays the change of channels at the boundary without a gap is
VQ116's to hear (idiosyncrasies.md, hls.js's entry). *Proven by:* web/packages/player/src/hls.test.ts
("keeps the sound loaded when its quality steps down to the light track, the new one loaded from its
end"; "plays a sound the person chooses at once, the loaded one thrown away"); VQ116.

## D369 — Every device plays with the app's own player controls, built from one standard set of player widgets

**Decided** (2026-10-27), by the project owner. On a computer the Play page used the browser's own video
controls: Space pressed whatever control a click had focused, and the arrows could not reach them (the
owner: "When I use arrow keys to navigate, it only outlines the whole video playback … I have no way to
get at the other overlay controls from the keyboard"); offered the app's own controls on computers too,
or the browser's kept, the owner chose the app's own ("go with option 1"). The UI widget audit
([ui-widgets-audit-2026-10-27.md](../design/research/ui-widgets-audit-2026-10-27.md)) found the player's
controls drawn separately by the TV overlay, the cast remote, Up next and Watch Together, with two
timelines and three ways into full screen, and proposed one set, the player's first; the owner agreed
its answers ([navigation-and-widgets-answers-2026-10-27.md](../design/plans/navigation-and-widgets-answers-2026-10-27.md)).
**Revises**
[D338](#d338--a-cast-goes-to-the-devices-tab-in-front-its-receiver-keeps-a-televisions-controls-and-leaves-by-back-or-a-double-ok-and-stop-casting-returns-it-to-the-page-it-was-on)
§5 in part: the television's controls become every device's.

1. **One set of player widgets:** colour tokens for what is drawn over a video; an icon button, one
   size (2.75rem, the status tray's too: the owner, "let's try sizing them the same as the others and
   see how that feels"); a `Timeline` in milliseconds, touched anywhere on a phone, its arrows
   commands on a TV; and one `PlayerControls` bar fed by the video it plays, or by a remote connection
   (a cast's remote, Watch Together's page). Each icon is drawn by `Icon`, none as a text character.
2. **Every device plays with that bar,** computers included, the browser's own video controls off: play
   and pause, the timeline, full screen, sound, subtitles, volume, as the TV overlay has them, reachable
   by the arrows and Tab, a mouse showing the bar and stillness hiding it. Space plays and pauses
   wherever focus is in the player (as built 2026-10-27).
3. **Play is a button like every other**, its colour the page's most important (the owner).
4. **A test holds each widget as the icon test holds `Icon`:** no range input outside `Timeline`, no
   player button drawn outside the set.
5. **The rest of the audit's set** (choosers replacing native selects, problem and loading lines,
   panels, every top-bar pop-up modal) follows in later batches as the owner orders them.

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-27. Built 2026-10-27 in `web/apps/web/src`: the over-video tokens in
`tokens.css` (`--color-on-video`, `--color-video-scrim`, `--color-video-card`,
`--color-video-control`, beside `--color-video-background`), every raw colour outside the tokens and
the gallery's posters replaced; `IconButton` (`icon-button.tsx`), one size of 2.75rem, the status
tray's signs too, its icons in `player-icons.tsx` (play, pause, the 10 s steps, sound, muted, full
screen, leave full screen, close); `Timeline` (`timeline.tsx`, with `ClockTimes` and `clockText`),
its touch handling in `range-touch.ts`, shared with `VolumeRange`; `PlayerControls`
(`player-controls.tsx`) fed by a `PlayerSource`, `useVideoSource` for a video here and the cast's
session in `cast-remote.tsx`; the TV overlay (`tv-controls.tsx`) and the cast remote rebuilt on it;
a computer's and a phone's controls in `page-controls.tsx`, the Play page's browser controls off
(`play.tsx`, `up-next.tsx`); and `/ui-gallery` showing the set. As built, where the decision left it
open: the subtitle, audio track, boost, levelling and sound offset controls stay under the film,

## D370 — A video a person has watched shows a white check in its poster's tray, and a person can mark it watched or unwatched on its page

**Decided** (2026-10-27), by the project owner: "do we have a way to show that a video has been watched?
… I'm imagining a checkmark (in the icon tray)"; on the research
([watched-marks-2026-10-27.md](../design/research/watched-marks-2026-10-27.md)), whose four questions he
answered as recommended, and: "Don't bother with any fading or greying for watched items. Just the
checkmark, like everyone else does. Maybe a white checkmark is less intrusive and would stop people
complaining?" (Plex's green corner checks drew "a sea of green check marks".) Until now nothing stored
or showed watched: "finished" was read from the person's current position, so a finished film restarted
and stopped early counted as unfinished again, and a series' progress and Next Up stepped back.

1. **Watched is kept per person, per title**: a video becomes watched when its person plays it to the
   finished threshold (`finished_after_percent`, 90%) or to its end, on any copy of it (D363); and when
   marked so by hand. Unattended plays and files of unknown length never make it watched. It stays
   watched when played again: a rewatch shows the check and its progress bar.
2. **The mark is a white check in the poster's tray of status cues** (D301 §4), the last of its icons,
   drawn by `Icon` in white, read aloud "Watched". Nothing fades or greys the poster. It shows on films,
   series, episodes' rows and other videos, never on extras.
3. **A series or a season shows the check once every episode in it is watched**; until then its existing
   progress bar says how far along it is. No unwatched counts.
4. **Marking by hand is on the title's, season's and series' pages, not the poster** (the tray's icons are
   never controls): "Mark as watched" and "Mark as unwatched", for one video, a season or a whole series,
   with Undo rather than a question. Marked watched, a video leaves Continue Watching and plays next from
   its start; marked unwatched, it is as never watched.
5. **Continue Watching, Next Up and a series' progress read watched**, not the current position alone,
   so restarting a finished film no longer unfinishes it.
6. **No switch to hide the marks yet**; it waits until someone asks.

**Proven by:**
- 1: internal/core/api/watched_test.go (TestWatched_APlayToItsFinishMarksItWatchedAndARestartKeepsIt: past 90% of a known length, to the end of an unknown one, never unattended or far into an unknown length, still watched after a restart), internal/store/migrate_0062_test.go (TestMigrate_Step0062KeepsWatchedWhatWasFinished); VQ89
- 2: web/apps/web/src/status-cues.test.tsx ("mark what its person watched with the white check…"), watched-mark.test.tsx (the rows, nothing faded), ui-gallery.test.tsx, icon.test.tsx, colour-tokens.test.ts; TestWatched_AnExtraIsNeverMarkedAndAnUndoCannotBeOfTheFuture; VQ89
- 3: TestWatched_ASeasonOrASeriesIsMarkedByHandAndCheckedOnceEveryEpisodeIs; watched-mark.test.tsx (a season's row); VQ89
- 4: TestWatched_AMarkByHandIsAFreshStartAndUndoPutsItBack, TestWatched_ASeasonOrASeriesIsMarkedByHandAndCheckedOnceEveryEpisodeIs, TestWatched_ASeriesNotReachedIsNoSuchSeriesToMark, TestReach_ALibraryTakenBackIsGoneAtTheNextRequestEverywhere; watched-mark.test.tsx ("marks a film watched at once…", the season and the series); VQ89 (by remote)
- 5: TestWatched_RestartingAFinishedEpisodeKeepsTheSeriesWhereItWas, TestBrowse_AListShowsHowFarThePersonIsThroughEach, TestMembersOf_ReadThePersonsPositionsAgainstTheThresholds, TestMembersAhead_StartAtThePersonsPlaceInTheOrdering, internal/core/interest's TestRaiser_* (Next Up read from the marks)
- 6: nothing built, as decided

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-27. Built 2026-10-27. The store keeps `title_watched` (step 0062,
checkpoint 48 unmoved): a person's `watched_at`, NULL while not watched, and `marked_at`, their last
mark by hand either way; the step keeps watched what was finished until then (a position past the
household's `finished_after_percent` of a known length, a `completed` event, `purged_watching`'s
completions). `internal/core/playback/watched.go` writes it: a report played to its finish
(`keepWatchedByPlay`, from `report.go`), a report with an unattended span marking nothing; and
`MarkWatched`/`RestoreWatched`, the mark by hand and its Undo, which puts back each title's mark as
the mark's answer gave it. `internal/core/library/watched.go` reads it (`IsBeforeMark`: a position
watched at or before the last mark counts for nothing, in Continue Watching, a list's film progress,
Next Up and where a play resumes, `resume.go`) and says what may be marked: a film, episode or other
video reached, never an extra (`TitleToMark`), and a series' or season's episodes with a file in the
person's ordering, present now (`EpisodesToMark`). Next Up orders finished members by when they became
watched (`Member.FinishedAt`), so a rewatch begun does not move it, the later of several marked at
once winning. The API (`internal/core/api/watched.go`): `PUT`/`DELETE /items/{id}/watched`,
`/collections/{id}/watched`, `/collections/{id}/seasons/{season}/watched`, each answering `previous`,
and `PUT /watched` to put them back; `isWatched` on list entries, Continue Watching's rows, a title,
a series, its seasons and episodes. The web client (`web/apps/web/src/watched-mark.tsx`): the check
(`WatchedIcon`, `--color-watched`), the tray's last cue in `status-cues.tsx`, on season and episode
rows on the tray's patch (`series.tsx`), and *Mark as watched* / *Mark as unwatched* with Undo on a
title's page (`title.tsx`), a series' top page and a season's page. Measured as D185 §2 did, at the
reference scale (`refscale_test.go`, a third of the plays finished): a 60-film page's watched marks
0.05 ms by their keys (D185's live rollup: 0.84 ms); a page of series' progress, now counting watched
episodes, 15.6 ms against 14.3 ms before, the count dominating, within the 50 ms page budget. As built,
where the decision left it open: episode rows gained the check, not a progress bar; a series' check on
its own page counts the episodes the ordering in use lists with a file, as its list's progress does.
Not seen on a device yet (VQ89).

## D371 — A session has a leader that plays as a device plays alone; everyone else catches up to it, and a cast takes its sender's part

**Decided** (2026-10-28), by the project owner ("yes, approved"), from the owner's question after a day of casting fixes to the Fire TV: "We're
able to play files seamlessly on the tv stick, so it's our methodology when casting that breaks things.
What is actually causing the problem, and do we really have to do things the way we're doing, or is
there a better way to achieve the same effect?" A cast was a Watch Together session of one (D88,
D364), so the receiver was steered by a group's sync: it waited for the group to be ready (D250 §2),
started at a scheduled moment with a run-up seek (D282), was held paused and sought back to the
group's place while it waited, was nudged by rate to the group's clock (D268), and the group waited
for it when it stalled (D247). With one screen there is nothing to keep it in step with, and each of
those moves (a seek, a pause, a rate change) costs a Silk device a refill: every cast bug of
2026-10-28 was one of them (the 0.9× nudge loop, the hold's seek back, the run-up's jump, the
play-pause-play start, the receiver never counted ready). The owner, agreeing: "Yes, the others
catching up makes more sense. Also, your better way makes sense."

1. **Every session has one leader: the screen that is the film.** It plays exactly as a device plays
   a film alone: it starts when it is ready, buffers as it needs, and is never held, sought to a
   group's place, run up or nudged. The group's position is the leader's.
2. **Everyone else catches up to the leader.** A follower seeks or nudges to the leader's position by
   Watch Together's existing catch-up (D250's "a member's trouble is theirs to catch up on", D268's
   correction). Nobody waits for anybody: the owner, "Let's make everyone catch up to the leader when
   they stall." This replaces D247's group waiting once for a stalled viewer, D250 §2's waits for
   members to be ready (and its 2026-10-28 amendment for a session's only player), and D282's
   scheduled start with a run-up for the leader; a follower may still run up to meet the leader where
   it helps it land in step.
3. **The leader is the host's screen**: the device the host plays on, in Watch Together the session's
   host, and alone the person playing.
4. **A cast takes its sender's part.** The owner: "We need to handle the leader casting, and also a
   follower casting. In each case the cast-to device behaves exactly as their main device would have.
   For the leader, his cast-to device becomes the leading device. For a follower, his cast-to device is
   just another follower." The sending device becomes a remote control (D88): play, pause, seek, the
   next item and stop go to the device it casts to, which carries each out as its own press, and that
   device's state (where it is, playing or paused, its quality and link) comes back for the sender to
   show (the owner's earlier ask, 2026-10-28: "The controller side should get information about
   playback, such as the transcoding and bandwidth choices").
5. **A cast alone is a session with a leader and no followers**, so it plays as the device plays a film
   alone. The hub and its connections stay the way commands and state travel (D364); what changes is
   that nothing steers the leader.
6. **The host's own start, in Watch Together, is the leader's**: it plays at once, and the guests
   catch up (the owner: "the others catching up makes more sense"), so no host's page plays, is held
   and plays again.

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-28; built 2026-10-28 in three stages. The first, the leader: the hub keeps
a leader for each session, the host's device that plays, the newest attached or the one that put the
film on, the next taking the lead as it leaves (`internal/core/together/group.go`: `lead`,
`leaderLeft`, `followLeader`; `hub.go`); the group's position is the leader's, placed by its state,
held where it stands while it loads or stalls, and the group waits for no one else (`settle`,
`endWait`, `stalled`, `dropped`, `followOnlyPlayer` and the sync wait gone, `together_sync_wait_seconds`
retired); a command of another device stands for the leader, which carries it out as its own press;
the roster says who leads (`isLeader`) and how each player plays (`playback`: delivery, quality,
link); the log says who leads at each change (`logEvent=leaderChanged`, `leaderDeviceId` on each
`groupChanged`). The web client's player leads while its roster says so
(`web/packages/sdk/src/together-leader.ts`, `together-follow.ts`), the only-player rule of an earlier commit
gone (`aloneCorrection`); the Play page says how the film is delivered (`deliveryOf`,
`film-player.tsx`), and the casting page shows the receiver's delivery, quality and link
(`cast-remote.tsx`). Its second stage, followers catching up, built the same day: a group plays at
once, with or without a leader, naming no moment to start at (`startOf`, `startsIn` and the
group's `startsInMs` gone, `together_start_lead_ms` retired); no player runs up or learns how late
it starts (`together-start.ts`, `StartLearner`, the `startLagMs` state and `orpheum.together.startLag`
gone, `together_run_up_ms` retired); a long jump is snapped to its keyframe itself; a follower held
while its group stands for its leader plays as the leader plays and is nudged or sought into step,
and catches up after a seek or a stall with the group told nothing; the core's log says each
follower's catch-up at info, by seek or nudge and how far behind the leader
(`logEvent=followerCaughtUp`, `player_log.go`). Its third stage, a follower's cast, built the same
day: a cast's receiver is handed its person's part in the Watch Together session they are in
(`Hub.TogetherPart`, replacing `HostedCredential`; `live.Registry.TakesPartBy`; the receive
message's `isTogetherFollower`), the host's leading it as before (D364 §11), a signed-in guest's
following it as just another follower: the receiver's ready page plays the group's film in the
guest's part (`FollowsTheGroupHere`, `cast-ready.tsx`, `together-viewer.tsx`), the guest's own
page, which now holds the live connection, leaves the film to it and holds the group's controls its
rights give, and the casting page leads to the session's page. Built 2026-10-28. Revisits D88,
D247, D250, D268, D282 and D364 as above, and D283 §2–§3 and D285 §1 with them. Revisited by D372
the same day: its §3, and the resolved points on which device leads, the leader leaving and which
part a cast takes.

Resolved in the build, where the decision left it open (say if any should go otherwise):
- **Which of the host's devices leads**: the newest that plays as it attaches, and the one that puts
  a film on as it does; as the leader leaves, the host's newest other player, or none. A guest's
  device and a panel never lead.
- **A group standing for its leader** (`Waiting`) is how "the group's position is the leader's" reads
  while the leader loads, stalls or is paused by its browser (a hidden phone's page): the followers
  hold where it stands, and the group plays from where the leader plays, at once, as it says it does.
  A remote's play stands for the leader too, until it plays.
- **The leader leaving a group that stood for it**: the group plays on from there for whoever plays
  still (D364 §15's "leaving the film no longer stops it"); with no one playing, it stands.
- **A leader joining a group under way far from it** (the host's player opened again on a film the
  group played on without it) takes the group's place once, as a film starts from where it is
  resumed; one that put the film on starts where it is.
- **The leader's own seek is not snapped to a keyframe** (D285 §1): it is already where it went; a
  remote's or a guest's still is.
- **What the remote shows**: "Plays the file as it is" or "Plays it converted", the quality the
  receiver began and the link its player estimated as it chose it (hls.js's or its own controller's
  estimate at the switch), not a running measurement.
- **No follower runs up** (§2 allows one "where it helps it land in step"): with no moment named, a
  follower plays as it hears the group play and its usual correction closes the gap, a nudge for
  the start lag of a few hundred milliseconds; a run-up would be a seek, which costs a refill. The
  learned start lag, kept per browser, is dropped with it.
- **A long jump's snap** to its keyframe keeps no run-up after the keyframe (D285 §1 had one).
- **Which part a cast takes**: the session the person hosts, else the newest they joined signed in
  as a guest; a guest who joined by a link alone, not signed in, cannot cast (casting needs the
  person's devices).
- **A guest's cast follows the group only while it plays nothing of its own**: a film the guest plays
  on their own Play page while casting still goes to the receiver as a cast of one, which it leads,
  as before; a guest cannot change what the group plays.
- **The guest's own page** stops its film while this device's cast is accepted (any cast), showing
  "Playing on ‹Device›" and the group's controls; the casting page leads to the session's page for
  a guest's cast with nothing of its own, as it does for a host (D364 §11). The receiver keeps its
  controlled mode (Back, a double OK) over the guest's film; taking control back ends the cast, and
  the receiver goes home, as from the ready page.

**Proven by:**
- 1: TestHub_TheGroupIsWhereItsLeaderIsAndAFollowersStallChangesNothing, TestHub_AFilmPutOnStandsForItsLeaderAloneAndPlaysAsTheLeaderPlays, TestHub_ACommandOfAnotherDeviceStandsForTheLeaderToCarryItOut, web/packages/sdk/src/together-leader.test.ts ("is never nudged, skipped or sought", "plays the film it put on as soon as the group stands for it"), web/apps/web/src/cast-receiver.test.tsx ("plays as the device plays a film alone while its roster says it leads"); VQ101
- 2: TestHub_AJoiningViewerHoldsNoOneUp, TestHub_ADroppedPlayerStopsNoOne, TestHub_AGroupWithNoLeaderPlaysAtOnceFromWhereItStands, TestHub_LogsEachFollowersCatchUpAndHowFarBehindItsLeader, web/packages/sdk/src/together-leader.test.ts ("is nudged to the leader's place", "is held where the group stands for its leader, plays at once as the leader plays", "after a seek, holds where the leader went", "after a stall, jumps ahead to catch up to the leader"); VQ102
- 3: TestHub_TheHostsPlayerLeadsAndAnotherTakesTheLeadAsItLeaves, TestHub_NoPanelLeadsAndAGuestsLeadsWhileNoneOfTheHostsCan (a guest leading revisited by D372)
- 4: TestHub_TheRosterSaysHowEachPlayerPlaysTheFilm, TestHub_ACommandOfAnotherDeviceStandsForTheLeaderToCarryItOut, TestCast_AHostsReceiverHasACredentialForTheirSession, TestCast_AGuestsReceiverTakesTheirPartAsAFollower, TestRegistry_AGuestsReceiverIsHandedTheirPartToFollow, web/packages/sdk/src/together-leader.test.ts ("carries out another device's pause, play and seek once each", "tells its session how it plays the film"), web/apps/web/src/cast-remote.test.tsx ("shows how the receiver plays the film", "leaves a guest's cast with nothing of its own to their session's page"), web/apps/web/src/cast-ready.test.tsx ("follows its person's Watch Together session as just another follower"), web/apps/web/src/together-viewer-cast.test.tsx ("leaves the film to the device it casts to"); VQ101, VQ103
- 5: web/apps/web/src/cast-receiver.test.tsx ("plays as the device plays a film alone while its roster says it leads"), TestHub_ACommandOfAnotherDeviceStandsForTheLeaderToCarryItOut; VQ101
- 6: TestHub_AFilmPutOnStandsForItsLeaderAloneAndPlaysAsTheLeaderPlays (no lead, the guest loading), TestHub_AGroupWithNoLeaderPlaysAtOnceFromWhereItStands, web/packages/sdk/src/together-leader.test.ts ("plays the film it put on as soon as the group stands for it", "is held where the group stands for its leader, plays at once as the leader plays"); VQ102

## D372 — A session's lead passes to its longest-present player while the host's screen is gone, and a person is in one session at most

**Decided** (2026-10-28), by the project owner, amending D371 the day it was built, before any device
had tried it. The owner asked: "Can we make it so that leadership (the clock master) passes down the
line (longest-running participant wins) until the leader comes back and catches up? [...] A guest can
only be in 0 to 1 view together sessions. While in a view together session and also logged in, they
are free to navigate and even view another video (which only shows for them). When they go back to
the view together screen, they catch up and play the shared video. If not logged in, they are free
to exit the page and come back to the page to catch up and view, so long as the watch together
session is still active and their membership is still valid (they haven't been kicked)." Agreeing
to the lead's reading of it ("Mostly agreed"), with: "Yes, we can use the core's clock. If the core
is gone, the watch together session is gone anyway. If someone leaves and rejoins, their seniority
value resets to the current time. This isn't about being fair; it's about using an easy signal of
reliability to decide who will lead the shared viewing. Transfer of leadership doesn't transfer
hoster privileges. The host always gets preferential treatment as leader. If everyone is gone, the
session pauses and eventually times out. Starting a new session (if things get out of sync) signals
an intent to end the old one."

1. **The lead passes down the line.** While no device of the host's can lead, the session's leader
   (D371 §1) is the player present longest without a break: a guest's device as readily as one of
   the host's. Seniority is the moment the core saw the device arrive, stamped by the core's clock
   at microsecond resolution; the core alone orders it, with no negotiation (the session ends with
   the core anyway). Ties go to the lower device id.
2. **Seniority resets on every return.** A device that leaves the session's page, loses its
   connection or is counted gone takes the current time as its seniority when it comes back: the
   owner, "an easy signal of reliability to decide who will lead", not fairness.
3. **The host is always preferred.** A device of the host's that can lead leads ahead of any guest's,
   whatever their seniority; among the host's own, D371's rule (the newest that plays, the one that
   puts a film on). The host's screen coming back catches up as a follower first and takes the lead
   back once it plays in step, so the film never jumps for its return.
4. **Leading is not hosting.** A guest's device leading carries the film's clock only: what the group
   plays, who is removed, the session's end and every other host right stay the host's (D371 §4's
   commands still go to the leader to carry out).
5. **Gone, for the lead:** a leader whose connection drops, which goes silent past a short limit, or
   whose page its browser pauses or hides (a locked phone) is gone, and the lead passes at once. A
   leader's stall is not: the group stands for it as D371 resolved, and its followers hold.
6. **To lead, a device must be on the session's page with the film playing.** A member elsewhere
   stays a member but cannot lead.
7. **With everyone gone, the session pauses where it stands** and ends by its idle end
   (`together_idle_session_end_hours`, D346), as before.
8. **A person is in one session at most**, as host or as guest. Starting a new session ends the one
   the person hosts (the owner: it "signals an intent to end the old one"); its guests are told it
   ended. Joining another session as a guest asks first: "Leave ‹session› to join this one?".
9. **A signed-in guest may wander** (next batch): they stay a member while elsewhere in the app, even
   playing another film, which only they see; the roster shows them away; opening the session's page
   again catches them up to the shared film.
10. **A guest by link alone may leave and come back** (next batch): their link keeps them a member
    while the session lasts and they are not removed; opening its page again catches them up.

**Confirmed** the same day, after the owner asked what a leader is for when guests catch up anyway
("should we make the leader catch up as well and not give special treatment?"), and was told: its
playing is never corrected, so one screen plays as a device plays alone, and its stalls alone hold
the group. The owner: "We'll make the host the preferred leader." The host browsing away from the
session's page (to find the next film, the owner's case) is §6: a device not playing the shared film
cannot lead, so the lead passes, and the host's device on its return catches up, then leads again
(§3); a host whose film plays on a device they cast to keeps that device leading as they browse.

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-28; §1–§8 built 2026-10-28; §9–§10 built 2026-10-30, below.
The lead (`internal/core/together/leader.go`): each device's seniority is the core's clock as it attaches, to
the microsecond (`arrivedAt`), stamped again as its page is shown after its browser hid it; a device
leads only while it plays the film on a page its browser shows (`canLead`); the host's player leads
as it attaches while the host's leads or none does or nothing is on, a guest's player while none
leads (`arrived`); a leader whose connection closes or goes silent (`Detach` with `GoneClosed`,
`GoneSilent`), whose page is hidden (a state's `pageHidden`, `takeVisibility`) or whose member is
removed hands the lead at once to the host's newest other player, else the most senior
(`leaderGone`, `nextLeader`); a host's player that came back while a guest's leads a film takes the
lead back once its state is in step (`takeLeadInStep`, `inStep`); with no one left who can lead, a
Watch Together group pauses where it stands (event `everyoneLeft`, replacing D371's `leaderLeft`).
Each `leaderChanged` line says `why` (`attached`, `putOn`, `noneLed`, `hostInStep`, `leaderGone`),
`goneBecause` and `goneLeaderWasHost` for a leader gone, the previous leader, whether the new one is
the host's, its `leaderSeniority` and `leaderPresentMs`. The web client: a follower on a handheld
says `pageHidden` in its state as its page hides and tells its state as it is shown; the host's
player following a guest's lead tells its state each second (`isHostAwaitingLead`); a guest's
leading player undoes a move its link withholds (`GroupLeader.undo`, a `sought` note
`why=undone`) (`web/packages/sdk/src/together-follow.ts`, `together-leader.ts`,
`together-connection.ts`). One session per person (`internal/core/together/places.go`): `Open`
ends the session the person hosts and takes them out of one they joined; `Join` is refused with
`InAnotherSessionError`, the API's `in_another_session` (409, its detail the other session's
`hostName` and `isHost`), until the join says `shouldLeaveOther`, the person known by their sign-in
or by the membership the browser keeps (`heldCredential`); the Join form asks first
(`web/apps/web/src/together-join.tsx`); `TogetherPart` takes the one session the person is in, and
`Opened.IsNew` is gone. Revisits D371 §3 (the host's screen leads; a guest's never did) and its
resolved points "which of the host's devices leads" (still so among the host's own), "the leader
leaving a group that stood for it" (the group now stands for the next leader, or pauses with no
one) and "which part a cast takes" (one session at most leaves one to take).

Resolved in the build, where the decision left it open (say if any should go otherwise):
- **"Silent past a short limit"** is the session socket's existing limit, three of the client's
  15 s pings (`silenceLimit`, 45 s), after which the device is dropped and the lead passes at once;
  no new number. A locked phone is caught sooner by its page's `pageHidden`.
- **Hidden** is said only by a handheld's page, where hiding pauses the film
  (`pageThatPausesWhenHidden`): a computer's hidden tab plays on, and may lead.
- **"In step"** is the follower correction's own threshold for needing no correction,
  `together_drift_left_alone_ms` (D250 §1), as the newest device brought it: ready, playing as the
  group plays (or held as it stands), within that of the group's position, its round trip allowed
  for. A host's player taking the lead back moves no one, and the group announces nothing.
- **The host's player attaching while a guest's leads and nothing is on** leads at once: there is
  nothing to jump. A host's player shown again after it was hidden is a return: it follows until in
  step, as one that reconnects does.
- **Everyone gone** is no device left that can lead (all gone, or every page hidden): a group that
  plays, or stands for its leader, pauses where it stands (`everyoneLeft`, "Everyone's screen left;
  paused at …"); a paused session ends by its idle end as before. A cast is not paused: a session of
  one, its receiver's return takes up where it stood.
- **A guest's leading player and its rights**: a pause or a jump its person makes that their link
  withholds is undone on that player, back to where the group is, rather than standing the group
  for it.
- **Starting a session while a guest in another** leaves that one too, without asking: starting
  one "signals an intent to end the old one", and a person is in one at most.
- **The join's protocol**: the core refuses with `in_another_session` and the join is sent again
  with `shouldLeaveOther`; leaving a session one hosts ends it for everyone, and the question says
  so ("Leave your own session to join this one? It ends for everyone in it."). A guest by link alone
  is known by the membership the browser keeps as the link's page loads (a link pasted into a tab
  already on another session's page forgets it first, as before, and is not asked).

§9–§10, built 2026-10-30 (the owner's item 7, navigation-and-widgets-answers-2026-10-27.md): a
signed-in guest's page (`/together`) is a screen in the shell, under the banner with its tray, menu and
Your account, in its one main landmark (`web/apps/web/src/app.tsx`'s `Screen`, `ViewerPage` in
`together-viewer-tap.tsx`); a guest by link alone keeps the bare page. Leaving the page closes only the
page's session connection: the membership stays the browser's (`orpheum.together.viewer`) and the
core's (a member is removed only by the host, by leaving, or by the session's end), so the guest goes
anywhere in the app, plays another film only they see, and comes back by the tray's Watch Together
sign (`/together`), whose page connects again by the kept membership and follows the group, catching
up (§3, D377 §3). A guest by link alone comes back by the same link in the same browser, as D267 §1
built it; in another browser the spent link is refused.

Resolved in the build, where §9–§10 left it open (say if any should go otherwise):
- **"Away"** is a member with no device on the session's page, whatever took it away: the roster
  cannot tell a guest who wandered from one whose page closed or whose connection dropped and was
  counted gone, and wandering is now the common case. Who is here says "‹name› (away)" (it said
  "(reconnecting)"); the host's list of people adds ", away" once the host's connection knows the
  roster (`together-news.tsx`, `together-people.tsx`). No new message or server state.
- **A signed-in guest playing another film** plays it as anyone signed in plays one, attached to no
  session: nothing of it reaches the group, and nothing new was needed.
- **Its debug tools**, on the bare page by link alone, are never shown (no person to choose them); in
  the shell, by the person's own Show debug tools, as on every signed-in page.
- **A spent link opened in another browser** is refused with the words every refused link has; the
  owner's distinct words for a used link (item 6) wait for the server to say "used" apart, not built.

**Proven by:**
- 1: TestHub_TheLeadPassesToThePlayerPresentLongest, TestHub_NoPanelLeadsAndAGuestsLeadsWhileNoneOfTheHostsCan, TestHub_TheHostsPlayerLeadsAndAnotherTakesTheLeadAsItLeaves; VQ104
- 2: TestHub_ADeviceThatComesBackIsPresentOnlySinceItCameBack, web/packages/sdk/src/together-lead-passes.test.ts ("tells its session as its page is hidden, where hiding pauses its film, and as it is shown again"); VQ105
- 3: TestHub_TheHostsPlayerComingBackFollowsUntilInStepThenLeads, TestHub_NoPanelLeadsAndAGuestsLeadsWhileNoneOfTheHostsCan, web/packages/sdk/src/together-lead-passes.test.ts ("follows as the host's player come back while a guest's leads, telling its state each second until it leads"); VQ104

- 10: web/apps/web/src/together-viewer-session.test.tsx ("comes back as the same member by the link it joined by, after the page was closed (D267 §1)"), web/apps/web/src/together-viewer-shell.test.tsx ("stays a page of its own for a guest by link alone: no banner"); VQ172

## D373 — No one's stall holds a Watch Together group: a leader stalled past a short grace passes the lead

**Decided** (2026-10-29), by the project owner, amending D372 §5 and D371's resolution that the group
stands for its leader's stall. After VQ125 (the host's Chrome, throttled, stalled and held everyone):
"I'm beginning to think that leadership should pass on without the host when the host stalls." Asked
whether the group should ever wait for anyone's stall: "I think that we can't maintain good UX if we
decide algorithmically to hold everyone up. If it's important enough, someone can ask to rewind."

1. **The group never waits for a stall.** Neither a leader's nor a follower's stall holds the others;
   a device that stalls catches up to the group once it loads again (D371's catching up), missing what
   played meanwhile. Whoever wants it seen again asks the host to rewind.
2. **A leader stalled past a short grace is gone, for the lead** (D372 §5 amended): the lead passes down
   the line (D372 §1) and the others play on. The grace keeps a seek's or a quality switch's brief stall
   from handing the lead back and forth; its value is set when built, with its reason recorded.
3. **The host is still preferred** (D372 §3): a host's device that stalled catches up as a follower and
   takes the lead back once it plays in step.
4. **Starting still waits:** a film put on, or a seek by the host, waits for the players to be ready as
   before (the start rule); only a stall during playing is no one's to wait for.

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-29; built 2026-10-29. A Watch Together group that plays no longer moves
to `Waiting` for its leader's stall (`internal/core/together/group.go`: `followLeader`); each
player's stall while the group plays is kept from its first state that says it buffers (`takeStall`,
the device's `stalledSince`), forgotten as the group stops playing, its loading then the start's
(`endStalls`), and logged as it ends, who and for how long (`logEvent=stallNotWaitedFor`,
`isLeader`, `stalledMs`). A leader stalled past `stalledLeaderGrace`, 3 s, hands the lead to the
host's newest other player, else the most senior, passing over any that stalls too, with no group
change announced (`internal/core/together/leader.go`: `passStalledLead`, `nextLeader` now taking
which devices may lead, run as any device's state or ping reaches the core); the log says
`why=leaderGone goneBecause=stalled goneLeaderWasHost=… stalledMs=…`. With no one else to lead,
the stalled leader keeps the lead and the group plays on. The host's player stalled follows and takes
the lead back in step (`takeLeadInStep`, `hostInStep`, as D372 §3 built it). The web client's
leader tells its state each second while it says it buffers (`tick`,
`web/packages/sdk/src/together-follow.ts`), so the core sees the grace pass. Revisits D372 §5
and D371's resolved point "a group standing for its leader" (its stall). Revisited by D374 the same
day: a leader that plays again within the grace now catches up forward to the group, which no longer
steps back to it (the resolved point "a leader's stall within the grace" below), and the cast's
exemption is one rule with any lone contender's (D374 §3).

Resolved in the build, where the decision left it open (say if any should go otherwise):
- **The grace** is a named constant, as D372's silence limit is, not a setting: 3 s, fixed by
  other values. A quality switch's or a short refill's stall waits on one chunk, 2 s of film
  (`hls_segment_length_seconds`' starting value), which a link that carries the film loads in less
  than 2 s; a stalled leader tells its state each second, so the core sees a stall up to 1 s late;
  3 s outlasts both. It is no longer than a follower's drift before it seeks rather than nudges
  (`together_seek_drift_beyond_ms`' starting value, 3 s): a leader that plays again within the
  grace steps the group back to where it is, by at most that, which its followers nudge across.
- **A leader's stall within the grace** leaves the group playing on, and the leader playing again
  places the group where it is, as each of its states does: the group steps back by the stall, its
  followers catching up to it.
- **A cast** keeps standing for its receiver's stall (`Waiting`, `waitingFor`): a session of one
  holds no one up, and its remote shows where the receiver is.
- **A leader paused by its browser** without buffering (not a stall) still stands the group as
  before; a hidden page is gone (D372 §5).
- **Starting**: what a player loads while the group stands (a film put on, a play, a seek) is the
  start's, not a stall, and its stall's clock starts only once the group plays.

**Proven by:**
- 1: TestHub_TheGroupIsWhereItsLeaderIsAndAFollowersStallChangesNothing, TestHub_ALeaderStalledPastItsGracePassesTheLeadAndTheGroupPlaysOn, TestCast_AReceiversStallStandsItsGroupForIt; VQ128
- 2: TestHub_ALeaderStalledPastItsGracePassesTheLeadAndTheGroupPlaysOn, TestHub_ALeadersStallWithinItsGraceKeepsTheLead, TestHub_ALeaderHiddenOrSilentIsGoneAndAStalledOneIsNot, web/packages/sdk/src/together-leader.test.ts ("tells its state each second while it stalls and its group plays on, by which the server hands its lead on (D373 §2)"); VQ128

## D374 — Only a device playing the film can lead; a cast's sender never does

**Decided** (2026-10-29), by the project owner, generalising D372 §6 for casting: "When we cast to a
device, that device becomes one of the contenders for "leader". There's no point in a device that
initiated the cast becoming leader because it has no video player to lead with. So: Only devices that
are actually playing video can be contenders for leadership."

1. **A contender for the lead is a device whose player is playing the session's film now**: attached
   in a playing role is not enough. A device whose film was handed to a cast receiver, whose player is
   gone, not yet loaded or showing another film, is passed over by every choice of leader (D372 §1, §3,
   D373 §2), the host's included; the receiver it cast to contends in its place (D371).
2. **The host's preference holds among contenders only** (D372 §3): a host whose film plays on a device
   they cast to leads through that receiver, never through the sender.

3. **With one contender left, its stall is waited for** (amends D373 §1): the owner, "When the leader is
   the only one left actually playing the video, the end-user behavior is that stalls don't cause it to
   jump ahead (because there's no one who would be affected). Playback waits when there is only one
   viable player." The group stands where its only contender stalled, as a film played alone does,
   and goes on from there; it never skips ahead on the group's clock. A cast's receiver, a session of
   one, is the same case (D373's build already exempted it).

Also agreed the same day, on D373's build: a leader that recovers within D373's grace catches up to the
group rather than placing the group back at itself, so no one sees a stretch twice.

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-29; built 2026-10-29. A player's state says the film it has (`fileId`,
0 for none), and a contender for the lead is a player on a shown page whose latest state, or the
film it put on itself, is the session's film (`internal/core/together/leader.go`: `contends`,
`whyPassedOver`); every choice of leader goes through it (`arrived`, now run as a device first
contends, `takeLeadInStep`, `nextLeader`, `passStalledLead`), and a leader that stops contending,
its page hidden, its player gone or another film's, hands the lead on at once (`takeContention`,
`goneBecause=noFilm`, `otherFilm`, `hidden`); a film put on, or stopped, hands on a lead that does
not play it (`filmChanged`). Each `leaderChanged` line for a lead handed on says each player passed
over and why (`passedOver="<device id>:<why> …"`: `noFilm`, `otherFilm`, `hidden`, `nothingOn`,
`stalled`). The guest's page while its device casts says it has no film (`tellsNoFilmHere`,
`web/apps/web/src/together-viewer.tsx`), and the web client's player says its film in each state
(`web/packages/sdk/src/together-follow.ts`). §3: the group stands for its only contender's stall
(`isOnlyContender`, `followLeader`), the cast's own exemption folded into it. The catch-up: a
leader's stall that ends within the grace while its group played on sets it catching up
(`catchingUpSince`, logged on the `stallNotWaitedFor` line with `catchesUp=true behindGroupMs=…`);
its states place the group only once in step (`leaderCatchesUp`, `logEvent=leaderCaughtUp`
`offGroupMs`, `catchingUpMs`), its catch-up moves logged as a follower's (`followerCaughtUp`
`isLeaderCatchingUp=true`); the web client's leader follows as a follower does until in step
(`LeaderCatchUp`, `web/packages/sdk/src/together-leader.ts`). Revisits D372 §6 and its resolved point
"the host's player attaching while a guest's leads and nothing is on" (with nothing on no one
leads now), and D373 §1 and its resolved points "a leader's stall within the grace" and "a cast".

Resolved in the build, where the decision left it open (say if any should go otherwise):
- **"Playing the film"** is the player having the session's film loaded, as its state says, whether
  it plays, buffers, or is paused with its group: a stall is D373's grace's to judge, and a paused
  group needs a leader for its play. The host's player that puts a film on contends for it at once,
  before its first state, so a film put on still stands for its leader while it loads (D373 §4).
- **With nothing on, no one leads**: there is no film to play. A film put on by a panel, no player
  of it yet, plays at once (D371 §2), and the first to play it leads.
- **A casting sender**: a host's Play page is left as the cast starts, so its video device's
  connection closes; a guest's page keeps its connection and now says it has no film. Both are
  passed over; the receiver, attaching as the host's player, leads once it plays in step
  (`hostInStep`) or, if the host's own still led, at once as the host's newest (`attached`).
- **A second contender arriving while the only one's stall is waited for** is held where the group
  stands, as every follower is, so the group goes on as its leader plays again; two contenders, one
  leaving while the leader stalls, the leader's next state (each second) stands the group where the
  leader is.
- **A lone contender catching up**: none, since its group waited for it.

**Proven by:**
- 1: TestHub_ACastingSenderNeverLeadsAndItsReceiverDoes, TestHub_APlayerNotPlayingTheFilmIsPassedOverForTheLead, TestHub_TheHostsPlayerPuttingAFilmOnLeadsItWhileItLoads, TestHub_NoPanelLeadsAndAGuestsLeadsWhileNoneOfTheHostsCan, web/apps/web/src/together-viewer-cast.test.tsx ("leaves the film to the device it casts to"), web/packages/sdk/src/together-connection.test.ts ("reports the player's state …"); VQ129
- 2: TestHub_ACastingSenderNeverLeadsAndItsReceiverDoes, TestHub_TheHostsPlayerLeadsAndAnotherTakesTheLeadAsItLeaves; VQ129
- 3: TestHub_TheOnlyContendersStallIsWaitedFor, TestCast_AReceiversStallStandsItsGroupForIt; VQ129
- The catch-up: TestHub_ALeadersStallWithinItsGraceKeepsTheLead, TestHub_TheGroupIsWhereItsLeaderIsAndAFollowersStallChangesNothing, web/packages/sdk/src/together-leader.test.ts ("catches up to its group after a stall the group played on through, nudged forward, then leads from there (D374)"); VQ129

## D375 — A session left with no player keeps its playing state, and goes on as it was when a leader returns

**Decided** (2026-10-29), by the project owner, amending D372 §7, after the Mac's Wi-Fi dropped both its
browsers with the S23 locked, the session paused for everyone's leaving, and both came back to a paused
film: "When a leaderless session gets a leader again, it should preserve playback state (position, and
play/pause)."

1. **Everyone gone holds the film where it stands, as it was.** The session stops the clock at the
   moment its last contender (D374 §1) went, and keeps whether it was playing or paused; it does not
   become paused for having no one.
2. **A leader's return carries on that state.** The first contender back leads (D372, D374) from that
   position: playing if the session was playing, paused if a person had paused it. Followers catch up as
   ever. No time limit (the lead's proposed 2-minute window was not taken).
3. **The idle end still applies** (D372 §7, `together_idle_session_end_hours`, D346).

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-29; built 2026-10-29. §1: the last contender gone, a Watch Together group
with a film on is held `Paused` where the core placed it then, its clock still, and keeps whether it
was playing or standing to play (`group.isHeldPlaying`, told as the group's `isHeldPlaying`) or a
person had paused it (`internal/core/together/leader.go`: `leaderGone`); the `groupChanged … event=everyoneLeft`
line says `heldPlaying=true|false` (`group.go`: `logChange`). A person's pause while it is held ends
the hold's playing (it is theirs now); a seek or a rate keeps it; a play, a film put on or a stop ends
it. §2: the first contender back, leading as none did (`arrived`), carries it on (`resumeOnReturn`):
held playing, the group stands where it held for its leader (`Waiting`, event `resumedOnReturn`,
logged with `positionMs`) and plays as the leader plays (`leaderPlays`), the start rule; held paused,
it stays paused. §3: a held group is not played to a player, so `EndStale` ends it at its idle end.
The web client follows a held group as any paused one, and says it is held and plays on when a
screen is back (`web/packages/sdk/src/together.ts`, `web/apps/web/src/together-events.ts`).

Resolved in the build, where the decision left it open (say if any should go otherwise):
- **The state** is `Paused` with a flag, not a new state: every client already shows a paused group,
  with no catch-up to a moving clock, and a new state would have reached every client's follow and
  lead; the event (`everyoneLeft`) and the flag say it is no person's pause.
- **Where the held film goes on from** is the start rule's: the group stands at the held position
  for its leader, and plays from where its leader then says it plays. A returning player farther from
  the held position than a follower seeks across seeks to it as it joins (`#joinAt`); one nearer
  plays from where it is, which places the group there.
- **A cast** is unchanged: its group plays on for its receiver's return (D372 §7), never held.
- **A lone contender's stall** (D374 §3) is unchanged: the one returning is its group's only
  contender, which the group stands for while it loads.

**Proven by:**
- 1: TestHub_AGroupLeftWhilePlayingIsHeldAndPlaysOnAsAPlayerReturns, TestHub_AGroupLeftWhilePausedStaysPausedAsAPlayerReturns, TestHub_WithEveryoneGoneTheGroupPausesWhereItStandsThenEndsIdle, web/apps/web/src/together-events.test.ts ("says a group everyone's screen left while it played is held …"); VQ134
- 2: TestHub_AGroupLeftWhilePlayingIsHeldAndPlaysOnAsAPlayerReturns, TestHub_AGroupLeftWhilePausedStaysPausedAsAPlayerReturns; VQ134
- 3: TestHub_AGroupHeldForWantOfAPlayerEndsIdle, TestHub_WithEveryoneGoneTheGroupPausesWhereItStandsThenEndsIdle

## D376 — A new leader that remembers its place sets the group's position; else the core's stands

**Decided** (2026-10-29), by the project owner, amending D375 §2 after its first device run (VQ134):
"having it playback from the core's remembered position feels weird. Whoever takes leadership role
should give their current playback position as the new official position."

Refined the same minute: "If the new leader remembers where its position should be (i.e. it was actually
playing, and isn't just connecting fresh while taking leadership), its position becomes the new official
position. If nobody can remember, then the core's current position remains the official one."

1. **A new leader that remembers its place sets the group's position**: a device taking the lead, for any
   reason (D372, D373, D374, D375), that was itself playing the session's film until then (a follower in
   step, a stalled leader's successor, a device back from a dropped connection with its film still
   loaded) makes its own current position the group's, and the others catch up to it as ever.
2. **A leader with nothing to remember keeps the core's position**: a device connecting fresh as it takes
   the lead (a reloaded page, a new player) takes the group's position from the core, as before.
3. **A session held with no player** (D375 §1) keeps whether it was playing or paused; the first contender
   back resumes it from its own position if it remembers one (1), else from the held one (2).

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-29; not built: replaced by D377 the same day.

## D377 — Who leads a Watch Together session, and from where: one procedure

**Decided** (2026-10-29), by the project owner, consolidating and replacing D372 §1–§3 and D376 (D373's
grace, D374's contenders and D375's held state stand, restated here where they meet). The owner proposed
the procedure ("I'm trying to think of a foolproof procedure for deciding who leads"); the lead named six
gaps with answers (1–6 below), and the owner agreed them all ("agreed").

1. **Contenders.** Only a device with a player open on the session's film that is playing or ready to
   play can lead (D374 §1): a cast's receiver, never its sender.
2. **Order.** The host's contender first (D372 §3); else the guest's contender with the earliest start of
   its current run. A run starts when the core hears the device playing or ready, stamped by the core's
   clock (never a device's); it ends, and the device goes to the back, when it disconnects, its page is
   hidden, it leaves the Play page or changes film, or it stays stalled past D373's grace. Connecting
   alone starts no run.
3. **The official position on connecting.** The core gives every connecting device the group's position.
   A device that was playing, or trying to, keeps where it was and waits to hear of the leader; while a
   leader exists, the device takes the leader's position.
4. **A device's own position becomes official only when no one leads.** Chosen to lead in a leaderless
   session, a device presents its own position if it has one, and the core takes it; if it has none (a
   fresh page), the core's stands. A handover from a live leader needs no position: the successor is in
   step. All others take on the leader's position.
5. **Play or pause is the session's, not the device's** (D375): a device presents its position only; a
   device paused by a dropped network, a locked phone or its browser does not pause the group. Only a
   person's Pause or Play changes it.
6. **The host returning takes the lead in step**: it first takes the current leader's position, then the
   lead, so no one sees a jump; after a leaderless race the first contender to present wins, and a host
   arriving later takes over the same way, without churn.
7. **No one left**: the session holds where it stood with its play or pause (D375), and rule 4 resumes it.

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-29; built 2026-10-29 (`internal/core/together/leader.go`). §1: `contends`, as
D374 built it. §2: each device's run (`runSince`) starts as its state first says it plays or is ready
with the session's film on a shown page, by the core's clock to the microsecond, and ends as it
disconnects (`Detach`), its page is hidden, its player has another film or none (`takeRun`), or it stays
stalled past `stalledLeaderGrace` (`endStalledRuns`), or, leading, paused by its browser past it
(`passStalledLead`); connecting starts none. The line is the host's newest contender, else the run that
started earliest, ties to the lower id, a contender with no run behind every one with one
(`isAheadInLine`, in `nextLeader`); the arrival seniority (`arrivedAt`) is gone. The log says each run's
start and end (`logEvent=runStarted runSince=…`, `logEvent=runEnded why=closed|silent|hidden|leftFilm|stalled|paused`),
and each `leaderChanged` line the new leader's `leaderRunSince` and `leaderRunMs` (or `leaderRunSince=none`).
§3: the web client's player (`web/packages/sdk/src/together-follow.ts`) that played the film with its
group on its page (`hasPlayedAlong`) keeps where it is on each new connection until its roster names a
leader (`LeaderAwaited`, `together-roster.ts`), so its first state at its welcome tells its own
position; once a leader is named it follows as any follower. §4: every change of leader goes through
`placeByNewLeader`, called by `lead`: chosen while no one led, a device whose latest state says it has a
position of its own (`remembersPlace`, sent once its player has played along, no older than the
group's last change) presents it and the group stands there; else, and on every handover from a live
leader, the core's position stands; each `leaderChanged` line says `positionFrom=leader|core`,
`positionMs`, and for a presented position `steppedMs`. §5: a leader's own pause, not a person's, no
longer stands its group (`followLeader`), unless it is the only contender (D374 §3), and past the grace
hands the lead to one that plays (`goneBecause=paused`). §6: `takeLeadInStep`, as D372 §3 built it, the
host's device taking no position as it takes the lead. §7: D375's hold, resumed by §4.

Resolved in the build, where the decision left it open (say if any should go otherwise):
- **"Has a position"** is the device's word (`remembersPlace`): a reloaded page and a device back from a
  dropped connection are both a new device to the core, and only the page knows which kept its film.
- **A contender with no run** (attached and contending, never yet ready) stands behind every one with a
  run, so a lone one still leads a group no one else can.
- **A leader paused by its browser** is judged by its last state's play and buffering, since its last
  change of either (`playerChangedAt`).

**Proven by:**
- 1: TestHub_APlayerNotPlayingTheFilmIsPassedOverForTheLead, TestHub_ACastingSenderNeverLeadsAndItsReceiverDoes
- 2: TestHub_TheLineForTheLeadIsByRunNotByArrival, TestHub_TheLeadPassesToThePlayerPresentLongest, TestHub_ADeviceThatComesBackIsPresentOnlySinceItCameBack; VQ139
- 3: web/packages/sdk/src/together-own-position.test.ts ("is kept on connecting again, …"), web/packages/sdk/src/together-connection-state.test.ts ("tells the group, in its first state at its welcome, …"); VQ139
- 4: TestHub_AFollowerTakingOverFromALiveLeaderMovesNoOne, TestHub_ALeaderlessGroupGoesOnFromThePositionItsNewLeaderPresents, web/packages/sdk/src/together-own-position.test.ts ("is one it says it has only once it has played along …"); VQ139
- 5: TestHub_ALeadersOwnPauseNeitherStopsTheGroupNorHoldsTheLead; VQ139
- 6: TestHub_TheHostsPlayerComingBackFollowsUntilInStepThenLeads; VQ139
- 7: TestHub_ALeaderlessGroupGoesOnFromThePositionItsNewLeaderPresents, TestHub_AGroupLeftWhilePlayingIsHeldAndPlaysOnAsAPlayerReturns; VQ139

## D378 — An unticked verification item is owed, not a failure; web reds are kept by their tests' modules

**Decided** (2026-10-30), by the project owner, amending D190's `Verified-By:` rule and the caching
audit's finding 3 (revert-red's record). The 10-27 batch's check-pr took 75 minutes and failed only on
files whose VQ items were unticked; the owner: "Sometimes it's better to push through a batch that's been
taking too long, even if it risks a bug getting through. We have the VQs as a record of things we need to
test but haven't yet, so we don't actually lose anything when pushing through anyway ... since I'm the
only one who controls what in the VQs pass, it doesn't make much sense for it to cause spurious failures
in the mechanical checks. What I actually need from them is to be able to ask you 'What are the tests we
need most for this batch, and which unfinished tests really need to get sorted out?'"

1. **A `Verified-By:` naming a VQ item in the queue passes revert-red, ticked or not.** A trailer naming
   no item, or one not in the queue, still fails. The probe still runs first, so a file a test covers is
   covered whatever its commit claims (an earlier commit's lesson stands).
2. **Revert-red lists the owed items**: after its verdicts, "Owed device checks", each unticked VQ item
   with the batch's files that rest on it. That list, with each item's text, is what the lead answers
   the owner's question from: which checks this batch needs most, and which owed ones must be done.
3. **A web red is kept by the modules of the tests it failed** (read from the run's output), what they
   import, relative and through the workspace packages, and the runs' configurations
   (`scripts/revert_red_web.py` `modules_read`), not by the whole web client's tree, which every web
   commit changed (140 related runs, half the 75 minutes). A test whose modules read files by a path no
   import names (node:fs, import.meta.glob), a red whose output names no test, and every web green keep
   the whole tree. A missed import would keep a stale red, which passes a file; the nightly
   `check-everything` trusts no record, so such a red lasts a day at most.

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-30.

## D379 — A series page shows its seasons as a row of posters

**Decided** (2026-10-30), by the project owner, revising D367 §9's season picker (a choice box). The
owner (2026-10-28): "I'm not sure I like having the season selection done as a choice box. Jellyfin
actually shows posters for the seasons in the season page." Shown two shapes, the owner took the
lead's recommendation ("follow your recommendations on those").

1. **One series page** (D367 §9 stands in that): above its episodes, a row of its seasons' posters, the
   specials last; a season without a poster shows a still of it, else the series' poster.
2. **Choosing a poster shows that season's episodes below** and replaces the history entry (D367 §2);
   coming back preselects the season of the episode left, that episode focused (D367 §9).
3. **On a TV the row is one focus row**, Left and Right along it, Down into the episodes.
4. Not chosen: Jellyfin's own shape, a grid of season posters whose each season is a page of its own,
   which costs an extra page and an extra Back for every episode chosen.

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-30. Built 2026-10-30, in `web/apps/web/src/series.tsx`: §1 is
`SeasonRow`, a `poster-row` of `PosterCard`s between the series' head and the season shown (the
choice box, `SeasonPicker` over `route-chooser.tsx`, removed), in the server's order, whose aired
order already puts the specials last (`internal/core/api/browse.go`, `browse_test.go`); each card
names its season and its episode count, carries the watched check over its poster (D370 §3) and is
marked `aria-current` while shown. The server stores no season poster (a season is no item, and
artwork rows belong to items; TMDB's season `poster_path` is in the stored record but never
fetched), so every season shows its still, in its poster's place as D362 §2 draws one, else the
series' poster; a season's own poster, when the server fetches one, goes first. §2 is the card's
`Link` with `isReplacing` (`PosterCard`'s `isReplacing`), and the return to the season and episode
left is D367 §9's `useSeasonReturnedTo` over `episode-reached.ts`, unchanged. §3 is the row's
`data-focus-container`, the season's Mark as watched set at its heading's far end
(`series__season-head`) so Down from the row lands in the episodes. Tests: `series.test.tsx`,
`series-page.test.tsx`, `input-rows.browser.test.tsx`; on a TV, VQ180.

Season posters built 2026-10-30 (the owner: "Get real posters"): a season's poster is an artwork row
of its series, of kind poster, naming its aired season (`artwork.season_number`, step 0064); TMDB's
`seasons[].poster_path` in the series' stored record is named at every pass
(`internal/core/providers/tmdb/works.go`), so a series matched before gets its seasons' posters at its

another ordering's groups have none. A card shows its season's poster, else its still with no "No

## D380 — A debug tool caps this tab's download rate, or drops its connection for a while

**Decided** (2026-10-30), by the project owner, on the lead's recommendation ("follow your
recommendations on those"). Chrome's DevTools throttling never reached the WebRTC carrier (VQ128's
run), so a slow or lost link could be tested only by turning Wi-Fi off or a phone's remote debugging.

1. **Under Show debug tools** (the person's own option), on the player: a cap on this tab's download
   rate (off, 0.5, 1, 2 or 5 Mb/s), and "Drop the connection for 10, 30 or 60 s".
2. **The cap is applied in the player's chunk fetch**, so every carrier, WebRTC and HTTP, is capped
   alike and the player's link estimate sees what a slow link gives.
3. **The drop closes every socket and carrier of the tab and refuses to reconnect for that time**, then
   lets them reconnect as after a real network loss.
4. **It lasts for the tab only, and says so the whole time**: a badge ("Throttled to 1 Mb/s") stays on
   the page while a cap is on, as a DevTools box left ticked once cost an afternoon (agent-failures A51).

**Status:** Built 2026-10-30. §1: `LinkDebugTools` under the Play page's player, a `DebugTool`
(`web/apps/web/src/link-debug-tools.tsx`). §2: `shapedLoader` wraps hls.js's chunk loader
(`web/packages/player/src/link-shaping.ts`), letting each load's bytes through no faster than the cap,
one load after another as one link, its stats saying them as they come, so the controller's estimate
and its watch on a chunk on its way see the slow link; `link-shaping.test.ts` (fake clock). A film
played as its own file, with no ladder, is the browser's load and is not capped. §3: `LinkDebug.dropFor`
(`web/apps/web/src/link-debug.ts`) closes every socket the tab opened (the live and Watch Together
connections), refuses its API requests, sockets and chunk loads until the time is up, then dispatches
the browser's `online`, so they reconnect as after a real loss; `link-debug.test.ts`. The loader's
WebRTC peer connection itself, which the client has no handle on, stays open: everything the client
sends over it is refused instead. §4: the cap is kept in the tab's session storage, and `LinkCapBadge`
says it above every screen while it is on; `link-debug-tools.test.tsx`. On devices: VQ177.


**Accepted gaps** (the owner, 2026-10-30: "agreed"): §3's drop leaves the loader's WebRTC connection
open, refusing what the page sends over it, as closing it needs the loader's interface; §2's cap does
not reach a film played as its own file, which the browser loads itself, nor the film page's warm-up
until a Play page has mounted in the tab. The last two are filed for later
(navigation-and-widgets-answers-2026-10-27.md).
