## D381 — The player chooses the quality it starts on, by the rule it plays by

**Decided** (2026-10-30), by the project owner, on the lead's recommendation ("follow your
recommendations on those"), amending D257 §2. On the Fire TV, A View to a Kill and The Kid
showed two or three black frames at their start: the server chose the first quality at 70% of the
remembered link (2.5 Mb/s), the player's own choice moved at once to 12.2 Mb/s, and a new
initialisation segment resets Silk's decoder (navigation-and-widgets-answers-2026-10-27.md, "A black
blip").

1. **The player chooses its first quality before it loads anything**, from the remembered link speed it
   is given (`rememberedLinkKbps`), by the same rule its quality choice plays by, so the first chunk is
   of the quality it plays and no switch lands as playback begins. Every quality choice goes through
   that one path (memory one-path-for-decisions; principles §11's one way).
2. **The server's choice (D257 §2) stays for a player that remembers nothing** and for Safari's
   playlist order, as its start.

**Status:** Built 2026-10-30. §1: the bitrate controller's starting ceiling (`QualityCeiling`'s
`#startingCeiling`, `web/packages/player/src/abr-ceiling.ts`) is `steadyLevel` of the remembered link
with nothing loaded ahead, the rule its next-chunk choice plays by, where the playback's own start
says so (`shouldStartByRememberedLink`): the Play page's own offer on its ladder and the film page's
warm-up (`film-player.tsx`, `watching.ts`); `abr-start.test.ts` (11.9 Mb/s remembered on Bond's ladder
starts on the 12.2 Mb/s rung, no switch). §2: a player with no remembered link, a stalled player's
lower quality (D253) and a start the page chose itself (a warm-up's settled quality, the debug top,
`isStartThePages`) start at `startAtBps` as before; Safari's native HLS has no controller and keeps its
playlist order. On the Fire TV: VQ176.


## D382 — A given-up chunk lowers quality only as far as the link's estimate carries, and a busy page or a first piece measures nothing

**Decided** (2026-10-30), by the project owner, on the lead's recommendation ("yes I agree with
those proposals in principle", then "Yes agreed"), amending D352 §4. On the Fire TV, file 5664 started
on its top rung (15.6 Mb/s, the link remembered near 20 Mb/s); three seconds in, a chunk had brought
128 KiB, one WebRTC piece, after two seconds, as the TV dropped 6 of its first 101 frames. It was
given up and measured as 680 kb/s, and the give-up chose by that one chunk's rate: the lowest rung,
400 kb/s at 360p, held for the 30 s hold though the next chunks came at 17–20 Mb/s (the owner, staging,
VQ176's round).

1. **A give-up chooses by the link's estimate**, the given-up chunk's sample counted in it, never by
   that chunk's rate alone: the chunk's rate says only whether to give it up. Every quality choice
   goes through the one estimate (memory one-path-for-decisions).
2. **A chunk's first arriving piece measures nothing**: a transport that delivers in pieces (the
   WebRTC path's 128 KiB) brings the first with the first byte, so a sample counts the bytes after it
   over the time after it. A chunk given up with only its first piece is stuck, not slow (D352 §4,
   bandwidth-sampling-2026-10-29.md P3).
3. **A busy page measures nothing**: a chunk whose arrival a long task overlapped (the browser's own
   50 ms, where it reports them) is no sample of the link and cannot cause a give-up; bytes the page
   was too busy to read say nothing of the link. Long tasks of 50 ms and more are noted, with the
   chunk they excused.
4. **Each of a solo play's quality steps reaches the core's log**, as Watch Together's
   `qualitySwitched` notes do; until now a solo step was told only beside a stall or a seek.

The decoder's own limit (a rung that drops frames, MediaCapabilities, Compute Pressure, and a simpler
codec at the same quality where the link can carry it, the owner's addition) is next batch's design,
after a probe on the Fire TV (navigation-and-widgets-answers-2026-10-27.md).

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-30; built 2026-10-30 in the web player, not yet on staging (VQ187): §1 in `abr-ceiling.ts` (`#givenUpLevel`), §2 in `first-piece.ts`, `abr-choice.ts` (`afterFirstPiece`) and `abr-on-its-way.ts`, §3 in `abr-busy.ts`, wired through `ChoosingOptions.longTasks`, §4 in `chunked.ts` (`stepAndLinkNoter`), all under `web/packages/player/src/`.

**Proven by:**
- 1: web/packages/player/src/abr-given-up.test.ts ("lowers a slow chunk's quality only as far as the estimate carries, …"); VQ187
- 2: web/packages/player/src/abr-first-piece.test.ts ("gives up a chunk that brought only its first piece as stuck, …", "measures a loaded chunk by its bytes after its first piece, …"); VQ187
- 3: web/packages/player/src/abr-busy.test.ts ("does not give up a chunk whose arrival a long task overlapped, …", "takes no sample of a loaded chunk whose arrival a long task overlapped"); VQ187
- 4: web/packages/player/src/chunked.test.ts ("reach the core's log among its link's notes, each marked a step"); VQ187

## D383 — Back or Forward never starts a film, and a receiver with no controller goes to the film's page

**Decided** (2026-10-30), by the project owner ("yes, build it", and the second point in their own
words). On the Fire TV, a page reloaded after a deploy while it received a cast came back as a plain
Play page of the cast's film; Back then landed on an older Play page in its history, which started a
film watched earlier, and again on the next Back (the owner, staging).

1. **A Play page reached through the browser's history (Back or Forward) does not play**: it shows
   its title's page in its place, Play first. A film starts only by a deliberate act: Play, a cast,
   Up next, or rejoining a Watch Together session.
2. **A page showing a cast with no one controlling it**, by whatever strange circumstance (a reload,
   a deploy, a session that ended unseen), goes to the film's information page, or, where the person
   may not see it, to the home page (the owner: "if it ever finds itself in a cast page with no
   controller due to strange circumstances, it should go back to the info page, or if it doesn't
   have access to it, to the home page").

**Proven by:**
- 1: web/apps/web/src/navigation.test.ts ("a Play page the browser's Back or Forward returns to (D383 §1)"), web/apps/web/src/play-back.test.tsx; on a device, VQ189
- 2: web/apps/web/src/cast-uncontrolled.test.tsx, web/apps/web/src/cast-receiver.test.tsx ("goes to the film's page, its receiving over, when its cast ended unseen with no one controlling it (D383 §2)"), web/packages/sdk/src/live-connection.test.ts; on a device, VQ189

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-30, and built (2026-10-30) in the web client. Point 1 in `navigation.ts`,
the one place a route is read from the history: a Play page the browser's Back or Forward arrives
at, by a popstate or by loading the page again (the navigation timing's `back_forward`), is replaced
by the title's page its Play page noted on its entry once its playback named it (`noteInPlace`, from
`play-up.tsx`), else home. Left open, and decided so: a reload of the Play page the person is on
plays on (a reload is no step of the history), and so does Up's own step back to the page a stopped
cast took over (D338 §1, the app's step, not the person's). Point 2: the live connection pings once
told the devices and knows by the answer, which the server sends after anything handed on
connecting, that no cast was handed (`isReceiveKnown`); a page loaded again while its tab received
a cast holds its film until then, and, handed none or one not taken (Not now), goes to the noted
film's page, or home on the ready page, with none noted, or on a 403/404 reading the title
(`cast-uncontrolled.ts`); a received cast's session ending other than by Stop casting, take-back or
a replacing cast (gone, its receiver gone too long) does the same. A history entry written by an
older client has no title noted, so its Play page reached by Back goes home. Device check: VQ189.

## D384 — A cast that ends sends its receiver home, and the page cast from stays the page it was

**Decided** (2026-10-30), by the project owner ("Yes do 1+2 this batch and 3 the next batch", and §3 in
their own words), amending D364 §10, D383 §2 and the sender's casting page (D337, D364), and, as §2 was
widened, Watch Together's pages (D364 §13–§15, D372 §9). VQ103's run on
staging: the S23, a Watch Together guest, cast to the Fire TV. Stop casting left the TV playing the film
under its own control. A second cast was taken back by the TV 40 ms after its Use (castId 74, 17:42:59;
again at 17:48:46, `by=historyBack`): the Use dialog's close stepped the history back, and the
receiver's page, just shown, took that step for the person's Back. A third cast left the S23 on a
casting page of its own, from which the way back to the group's film went through "Go to Watch
Together's controls" and "Back to video" to the casting page again ("This is so confusing that I think
we need to fix it in this batch").

1. **A cast that ends sends its receiver to its home page**: Stop casting, the session's end, its
   controller gone, or a receiver found with no controller (replacing D383 §2's film page, the owner:
   "it's probably best from a UX perspective for a castee to go back to the home page whenever its
   cast ends. Otherwise it's too difficult to decide what it should do"). Taking control back on the
   receiver (Back, OK twice) is not an end: the film plays on there (D338, settled).
2. **The page cast from stays where it is**: a solo Play page or a Watch Together page keeps its
   place; its video's area says "Playing on ‹device›" and its controls work the receiver; Stop casting
   brings the film back to that same page. The tray's Cast opens a dialog to choose a device or stop,
   and never navigates. There is no casting page of its own. **Widened the same day**, by the owner:
   "Both cast and watch together should be modal dialogs, so this should all be done at once. Watch
   together keeps track of the shared video being played and offers a way to get back to it, but
   ultimately there is one playback page that everything goes through." So the tray's Watch Together
   opens a dialog too, never a page: starting a session, inviting (the links, who joined, removing),
   the people, voice and the volumes, Stop for everyone, and, while the session plays a film, "Back to
   the film", to its Play page. The Play page is the one page every film plays on: solo, the group's
   film for its host or a guest, and while its device casts. An old address of the Watch Together or
   casting page goes to the Play page of the film the session or cast plays, else home, Watch
   Together's dialog open where it was its page.
3. **No device in the same Watch Together session, controller or player, is a cast target** (next
   batch).

Also: a receiver ignores the history steps the app makes itself (a dialog's close): only the person's
own Back takes control back.

**Proven by:**
- 1: web/apps/web/src/cast-to.test.tsx ("goes to its home page in the page's place as a cast ends there, through the cast handed again with another film (D384 §1)", "goes home as casting ends, and Back from there never plays the cast's film (D384 §1, D383 §1)"), web/apps/web/src/cast-receiver.test.tsx ("goes home when the remote stops casting (D384 §1)", "goes home, its receiving over, when its cast ended unseen with no one controlling it (D384 §1)"), web/apps/web/src/cast-ready.test.tsx, web/apps/web/src/cast-uncontrolled.test.tsx, web/apps/web/src/cast-receiving-mark.test.ts, web/e2e/cast.spec.ts; on a device, VQ190
- 2: web/apps/web/src/cast-to.test.tsx ("a film played on a device that casts"), web/apps/web/src/cast-remote.test.tsx, web/apps/web/src/cast-dialog.test.tsx, web/apps/web/src/status-tray.test.tsx, web/apps/web/src/watch-together.test.tsx, web/apps/web/src/together-guest-play.test.tsx, web/apps/web/src/together-viewer-shell.test.tsx, web/apps/web/src/together-viewer-cast.test.tsx, web/apps/web/src/input-pages.browser.test.tsx, web/e2e/cast.spec.ts, web/e2e/together.spec.ts; on devices, VQ190
- Also: web/apps/web/src/cast-receiver-steps.test.tsx ("keeps control through the step the Use question's close makes, and leaves at the Back after"), web/apps/web/src/navigation.test.ts ("the person's own steps through the history"); on a device, VQ190

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-30; §1, §2 and the Also built (2026-10-30) in the web client, §3 not built
(the next batch). The Also in `navigation.ts`: navigation tells the person's own steps through the
history alone (`onPersonsStep`), never the end of a step the app makes itself off an entry held over
the page (a dialog's close), a go waiting on it, or Up's way back, nor a Back that only closed what
was open; the receiver's controlled mode listens there instead of to the window's popstate
(`cast-receiver.tsx`). Point 1 in `live.tsx`: every end of a received cast but control taken back
here sends the receiver home in the page's place, out of full screen (`leaveReceiving`), the ready

the page before a cast (`cast-return.ts`, `leaveTheCastsEntries`) and the film's page of D383 §2

`cast-dialog.tsx`, `together-dialog.tsx`, loaded as first opened, `tray-dialog-code.tsx`), each
closed as the page moves to another address; a Play page whose film goes to a receiver, sent on or
taken by a cast started over it, shows the cast's remote where its video was (`cast-to.tsx`'s
`PlayOrSendOn`, `cast-remote.tsx`'s `CastRemote`), and plays the film again from where the receiver
stood once the cast is stopped; a signed-in guest's Play page of the group's film follows it
(`together-guest-play.tsx`, `together-viewer.tsx`'s `GroupFilmPage`); `/casting` and
`/watch-together` go on as old addresses (`old-addresses.tsx`). Left open, and decided so: Cast's
dialog closes once a cast started from it is taken, the page under it the remote then; it keeps
"Back to the film" while a cast plays a film other than the page's; Watch Together's dialog holds no
remote of the group's film, its Play page holding the controls; while Watch Together is hosted, the
cast's remote on the Play page works the hosted session, the receiver its host's player (D364 §11);
a cast that moved on to another film comes back on that film's Play page, in the page's place; an
old `/casting` address goes to the cast's film, never the film it was opened from, so no film starts
by Back (D383 §1); a signed-in guest's voice, own volume and Leave stay under the group's film on its
Play page, where their voice already lived, rather than in the dialog, which for them holds the way
back to the film; a guest by link alone keeps their page of its own, which shows none of the app
(D246 §3), and is the one page their film plays on; a page of the group's film opened by a press
asks for no tap to continue. Device check: VQ190.

## D385 — A receiver that takes control back ends the cast: it goes home, and the sender plays on from where it stood

**Decided** (2026-10-30), by the project owner, amending D338 (settled 2026-10-27: a receiver taking
control back stays on the video) and D384 §1. On staging, after a Fire TV took control back, the
sender's page offered "Play here from ‹time›", its time rising on its own whatever the TV then did:
"This will get very confusing. I think there are too many weird edge cases if we allow the castee to
continue playback after taking back control from the caster. Let's just make the castee go back to the
home page, and the caster takes over the castee's playback state, as the controller + playback
device."

1. **Taking control back on the receiver (Back, OK twice) ends the cast like any other end**: the
   receiver goes to its home page (D384 §1, now without exception).
2. **The sender takes over the receiver's playback state** as the one controlling and playing
   device: its Play page plays the film from where the receiver stood, playing or paused as the
   receiver was, with no "Play here from" offer. In Watch Together, the sender's device becomes the
   member's player again (D364 §11).
3. **A receiver that loses its network ends the cast the same way, once the core is sure it is
   gone** (added the same day, by the owner: "We'll also need to handle the real edge case of a
   castee that loses network. The caster doesn't need to get its position exactly right. We could
   just have it take over at the last known playback position once it's sure the castee is gone."):
   the core's own judgment ends it, its receiver with no connection for `ReceiverGoneAfter` (D364
   §6, reason `receiverGone`), and the sender takes the film over as in §2, from the receiver's last
   known position, playing or paused as it was. A receiver back after that has no cast, and goes
   home (D384 §1).

Also (the owner, the same day): **ending a Watch Together session from its dialog closes the dialog**,
and nothing reopens it.

**Proven by:**
- 1: web/apps/web/src/cast-receiver.test.tsx ("ends the cast as its control is taken back here, and goes home once it has ended, the film as it stood until then (D385 §1)", "leaves Back to leave controlled mode, the sound still off", "takes control back at once when a Fire TV's Back or Escape leaves full screen, telling the log"), web/apps/web/src/cast-to.test.tsx ("goes home, forgetting it received, as its control is taken back here (D385 §1, amending D338 §6)"), web/e2e/cast.spec.ts; on a device, VQ190
- 2: web/apps/web/src/cast-remote.test.tsx ("plays the film here at once from where the receiver stood, paused as it was, as control is taken back there, offering nothing (D385 §2)", "plays the film of another page on that page, in this one's place, where the cast moved on to it, paused as the receiver had it", "waits paused there where the receiver had the film paused as its sender took it over, and plays at once where it played (D385 §2)"), web/apps/web/src/router.test.ts, web/e2e/cast.spec.ts; on a device, VQ190
- 3: web/apps/web/src/cast-remote.test.tsx ("plays the film here, playing, from where the receiver last stood once it is gone, not where the clock has moved it to since (D385 §3)"), cmd/orpheum/casts_gone_test.go, internal/core/live/registry_test.go (the core's end, unchanged); on a device, VQ190
- Also: web/apps/web/src/status-tray.test.tsx ("closes Watch Together's dialog as the session is ended from it, nothing opening it again, the page where it was (D385's Also)"), web/e2e/together-pages.ts (every Watch Together browser test that ends its session); on a device, VQ190

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-30; §1–§3 and the Also built (2026-10-30) in the web client, the core
unchanged. §1 in `cast-receiver.tsx`: control taken back ends the cast as `takenBack`
(`useTakingBackEnds`), and the receiver goes home through `live.tsx`'s `leaveReceiving` once the
server has answered or its session says the cast ended, whichever comes first, leaving the film as
it stands until then so the session holds it as the receiver left it for the sender;
`useEndsAsTheCastDoes` sends it home at every end but `replaced`. The film played on after taking
back is gone (`Receiving.onOver`, Live's `endReceiving`). §2 and §3 in `cast-remote.tsx`: `takenBack`
and `receiverGone` join `stopped` among the ends after which the Play page plays the film itself at
once (`useTakesTheFilmOver`), from where the receiver last stood while a device led the session the
remote works (`useWhereItStood`; the hosted one while Watch Together is on, so the sender's player
leads it again as the Play page's `HostPlaysTogether` does), paused where it was paused, through the
path Stop casting already used (`PlayOrSendOn`'s `playHereFrom`, now carrying `isPaused` to the Play
page's first ask, `Opened`'s `isStartPaused`; the play route's `paused=1` where the cast had moved
on to another film). §3 uses the core's existing end: a cast's session is not held for want of a
player, its clock running on after the receiver's connection is lost, so the last position is taken
where the server detached the receiver and no device led any more, at most the core's 45 s of
silence late, never the two minutes after. The Also in `watch-together.tsx` and
`together-dialog.tsx`: ending the session from the dialog closes it once the session is forgotten
(`WatchTogetherControls`' `onEnded`); before, the dialog stayed open and showed Start a session in
the session's place, which read as the dialog closing and opening again. Left open, and decided so:
Stop casting still plays the film here playing, whatever the receiver was doing (D384 §2 as built;
the server's answer says whether it played, should the owner want it paused as it was); "Play here
from" stays for the two ends the sender did not choose and cannot take over from, another device
taking the receiver (`replaced`) and the server no longer knowing the cast (`gone`); a sender not on
the cast's Play page as it ends plays nothing, as for Stop casting; the receiver's take-back no longer
names who took control back on the sender's page, which plays the film at once instead. Device
check: VQ190.

## D386 — A device receiving a cast is no one else's cast target, and a cast the server no longer knows sends its page home

**Decided** (2026-10-30), by the project owner, amending D364's replacing cast (VQ142's second case)
and D385's two remaining "Play here from" ends.

1. **While a device receives a cast, no other device may cast to it** until that cast ends: it is not
   offered as a target, and a cast to it is refused (the owner: "Don't let other devices take over
   casting. When a device is being cast to, no other device may cast to it until the current casting
   ends"). The person's own replacing cast (D364's `replaced=1`) goes with it.
2. **A cast the server no longer knows sends the page home with an error message**, sender or
   receiver (the owner: "For extreme edge cases like this, it's usually best to just go home"). With
   §1 and D385, "Play here from" has no end left to offer it, and goes.

**Status:** Decided 2026-10-30; not built yet.
